Sobre a empresa:

O Leevin Group atua no setor de acomodações para estudantes, tanto de curto quanto de longo prazo. Fundada em 2018, em Dublin, com o objetivo de oferecer aos estudantes serviços de hospedagem confiáveis e com ótimo custo-benefício. Nossa missão é proporcionar a todos os nossos clientes uma experiência única e satisfatória durante sua estadia na Irlanda. Estamos em busca de um(a) Community & Customer Experience Junior para apoiar diretamente a gestão da nossa comunidade de moradores e fortalecer a experiência do cliente dentro das propriedades.

Essa posição atua como ponto de contato entre residentes e time de CX, garantindo comunicação clara, organização de processos e resposta dentro de SLA, além de apoiar na prevenção de conflitos e reforço educativo das regras da casa.

Principais responsabilidades:

• Atuar como ponto de contato comunitário entre moradores e CX;

• Garantir respostas dentro do SLA;

• Reforçar House Rules e License Agreement de forma educativa;

• Orientar residentes sobre processos (maintenance, cleaning, replacement, notice etc.);

• Monitorar conflitos e atuar preventivamente;

• Identificar padrões recorrentes de reclamações;

• Manter registros organizados (Freshdesk / DM);

• Trabalhar em conjunto com Property Management, Sales e Collections;

Hard skills:

  • Fluência em inglês;
  • Experiência mínima de 1 ano em customer experience, suporte a hóspedes ou community management;
  • Capacidade de gerenciar múltiplos canais simultaneamente (chat, e-mail, tickets);
  • Familiaridade com ferramentas digitais: Freshdesk, suite Zoho, WhatsApp Business, Google Workspace;
  • Espanhol é diferencial real.

Soft skills essenciais:

  • Organização e capacidade de priorizar múltiplos casos abertos sem perder contexto;
  • Comunicação calma, clara e estruturada;
  • Resiliência emocional e foco na solução sob pressão;
  • Capacidade de manter limites com gentileza;
  • Postura respeitosa mesmo em situações de emergência.

Detalhes do contrato:

  • Modelo de contratação: PJ
  • Local: Brasil (100% remoto)
  • Escala: Segunda a Sexta · Das 07h ás 16h
  • Remuneração: R$5.000,00

jobs.excerpt: About BJAKThe original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money.
jobs.description:
About BJAK

The original mission of BJAK is we believe people deserve smarter ways to plan, save and grow their money. This is the origin of our name.

Started in 2019, we built the first mobile-first, insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, its the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

Today, we are expanding ways to help people in the region — this includes spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more. Our mission is help people get more from their money every day.

We have teams working around the world, with over 20 nationalities from our offices and remotely, who truly enjoys their work. We are looking for the most talented and driven people we can find. We are looking for people who work for their passion, not counting hours. Who loves building great next-generation products, not status quo. Who cares about redefining how everyone around us can get the best financial applications, not for an exclusive few.

If you're this person, we'd love to talk to you.

The Role

We are looking for a Business Unit Head to build and lead a business from end to end.

You will own the P&L, product, team and execution. You will identify opportunities, decide what to build, hire the team, launch and improve products, and drive growth and profitability.

This is a hands-on operating role with direct accountability for business results.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Own P&L, business strategy, targets and overall performance

  • Identify customer needs and commercial opportunities, and decide what products and features to build

  • Work directly with product, engineering and design teams to build and launch products

  • Build the team - hire strong people, set clear goals and manage performance

  • Drive user growth, engagement, revenue and profitability

  • Build partnerships and operations required to launch and scale the business

  • Make decisions quickly, solve problems directly and own execution from idea to results

What We're Looking For

  • Strong track record building, launching or scaling a product, business or business unit

  • Experience owning P&L, revenue, growth or other measurable business outcomes

  • Strong product and commercial judgement

  • Ability to work across product, engineering, operations and commercial functions

  • Experience building and leading strong teams

  • Hands-on approach - comfortable moving between strategy and detailed execution

  • Strong ownership, speed and ability to operate with limited structure

  • Experience in fintech, consumer technology or AI is an advantage

jobs.description:
** Open to remote within the West Coast only**

At JFrog, we’re reinventing DevOps to help the world’s greatest companies innovate -- and we want you along for the ride. This is a special place with a unique combination of brilliance, spirit and just all-around great people. Here, if you’re willing to do more, your career can take off. And since software plays a central role in everyone’s lives, you’ll be part of an important mission. Thousands of customers, including the majority of the Fortune 100, trust JFrog to manage, accelerate, and secure their software delivery from code to production -- a concept we call “liquid software.” Wouldn't it be amazing if you could join us in our journey?

As a Strategic Solution Architect, Presales at JFrog's Strategic Solution Engineering Team, you will be on the front lines, working closely with our top Fortune 500 customers, guiding them on how to build robust software delivery processes. You will work with our sales, product & engineering, customer success and marketing teams to help customers understand the value of JFrog solutions from a technical and business perspective.

If you love working with brilliant people, being part of an energetic team, changing the world of software and you’ve got the technical skills, you might be the perfect Frog to join our Swamp! Come and help us to continue to lead the rapidly evolving space of DevOps, DevSecOps and MLOps!

As a Strategic Solution Architect, Presales in JFrog you will...

  • Engage with JFrog’s most strategic customers to ensure their success in their DevSecOps journey leveraging JFrog’s products
  • Partner with Sales account executives to build accounts strategy, activities and build long lasting trust relationships with assigned JFrog customers
  • Educate customers (engineers and executives) on the JFrog platform fundamental capabilities and key value proposition across all the platform's broad set of capabilities
  • Represent JFrog in customer and public events and conferences
  • Work closely with Product & Engineering global organization to provide first hand feedback from the field and influence the Products features and roadmap based on insights gathered from customers
  • Keep current with the latest technology trends related to the DevOps, DevSecOps, MLOps and IoT landscapes
  • Collaborate with Customer Success and Marketing to broaden our customer engagements horizontally and vertically and increase the customers’ adoption of the JFrog Platform
  • Build relationships with key decision makers, visiting customers on-site, and serving as a customer's trusted technical point of contact

To be a Strategic Solution Architect, Presales in JFrog you need...

  • 10+ years experience in enterprise presales/solutions engineering for Fortune 500 / 100 accounts with multi million dollar deals
  • Superb interpersonal, team playing, show and tell style, customer happiness obsession and “can do” attitude
  • Extensive customer-facing experience in a software infrastructure enterprise presales role
  • Docker, Kubernetes, CI, git , Artifactory, Build tools (maven, gradle, npm, docker etc.)
  • Ability to build software delivery pipelines with Docker, npm, Java, Pypi etc. with various DevOps tools
  • Knowledgeable of application security (AppSec)
  • Hands-on experience in Linux - Mandatory
  • Hands-on experience with cloud infrastructure - AWS / Azure / GCP - Mandatory
  • Experience with software development in scale, both on-premise and in the cloud
  • Experience with Software Architecture design, product development, IT infrastructure a plus
  • Ability to travel at least 50% throughout the US
  • Uncompromising will to learn
  • Bachelor’s Degree or higher education in Computer Science/Engineering Major is preferred

WHAT JFROG CAN OFFER…

  • Open to remote work for candidates outside a reasonable commuting distance to the Seattle or Sunnyvale office.
  • At JFrog, base salary is only one component of our compensation package.
  • This position has a base salary range between $195,000 to $215,000. Base salary will be based on your skills, qualifications, experience and location.
  • Additionally, this role may be eligible for discretionary bonuses or commission payments.
  • This position also includes an equity package of restricted stock units (RSU). In addition, JFrog employees are eligible to participate in our Employee Stock Purchase Plan.
  • JFrog provides employees comprehensive benefits including medical, dental, vision, retirement, wellness and much more!

SUMMARY

We're looking for a Total Rewards Leader to support our compensation, equity, retirement programs, and total rewards strategy. You'll partner closely with HR, Finance, and business leaders to shape programs that help us attract, retain, and reward the people who make our staffing business run from internal associates to the talent we place every day.

Location: Remote

ESSENTIAL DUTIES and RESPONSIBILITIES

Include the following. Other duties may be assigned.

  • Manage compensation programs, including market benchmarking, salary structures, job evaluation, pay equity analysis, and annual compensation planning.
  • Support the Company’s 401(k) plan and support related audits and compliance requirements.
  • Support and lead a team of individual contributors to ensure seamless administration and delivery of Total Rewards programs.
  • Partner with HR, Payroll, Finance, and business leaders to improve processes, systems, and the overall employee experience.
  • Champion a culture of wellbeing and recognition by creating, communicating, and enhancing
  • Optimize HR systems and processes to provide seamless access to Total Rewards programs, reduce manual intervention, and enhance employee experience.
  • Ensure compliance with applicable federal and state employment laws, regulations, and reporting requirements related to compensation, equity, and Total Rewards programs.
  • Develop service level agreements to establish a results-driven service model, serve as the primary point of contact for escalations, and oversee quality assurance.
  • Identify opportunities, lead automation, and efficiency initiatives and projects.
  • Ensure business continuity through cross-training and process documentation of key processes for all benefit areas.
  • Manage relationships with vendors and recordkeepers.
  • Develop and maintain regular reporting on compensation, equity, and various Total Rewards programs and compliance requirements.

CORE KNOWLEDGE and SKILLS

  • Exceptional communication, relationship-building and analytical skills, with the ability to translate complex Total Rewards concepts into clear, compelling insights and build alignment across diverse stakeholders, including executive leadership.
  • Proven ability to leverage data, market intelligence, external benchmarks, technology and systems to inform strategy, drive innovative program design, optimize total rewards programs and enhance the employee experience.
  • Experience using AI tools (Claude) and other AI tools specific to Total Rewards a plus
  • Strong knowledge of applicable benefits and compensation regulations
  • Proficiency in Excel, HRIS platforms, and compensation management tools is required.

Leadership Competencies:

  • Intentional Collaboration & Synergy Building- Demonstrated ability to cultivate purposeful collaboration and synergies among internal and external stakeholders through a strategic and thoughtful approach.
  • Empathy and Emotional Intelligence - Demonstrate empathy and emotional intelligence to better understand employee concerns about benefits and sensitive situations, approaching interactions with compassion.
  • Adaptability - The ability to adjust to changes in vendors, regulations, and employee needs while thriving in fast-paced environments filled with uncertainty.
  • Candor - Comfortable working in a culture that values transparency and is committed to sharing and receiving meaningful feedback for collective improvement.
  • Service mindset- This mindset emphasizes prioritizing the needs of others, fostering a culture of service, and empowering individuals to perform at their best. By leading through example, it inspires mutual support and respect and creates a positive environment where everyone feels valued.

EDUCATION and EXPERIENCE

  • 5+ years of leadership experience
  • 6+ years of Total Rewards experience, compensation and equity analysis experience preferred.
  • Bachelor’s degree preferred.
  • CEBS, CCP, CBP, SHRM-CP/SCP, PHR/SPHR, or similar certification is a plus.

SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This position will directly manage small team of individual contributors.

Salary Range: $112,000 - $134,000 annually, depending on experience and geographic location plus eligibility for an annual bonus, subject to plan terms.

Please note that actual compensation offered may vary based on local pay requirements, and will meet or exceed state-specific minimum wage or salary thresholds.

Benefits and Well-Being:

We offer a competitive benefits package, including 6 paid holidays, 1 paid floating holiday and up to 20 days of Paid Time Off per year, Medical/Dental/Vision insurance, Company-matching 401(k) and Employee Stock Purchase Program, in addition to other programs and perks. More details about our benefits can be found here.

jobs.description:
Data Engineer V


Leads the technical direction, delivery standards, and day-to-day execution of a data engineering pod — spanning core EDW pipelines and AI/RAG data infrastructure — translating stakeholder needs into a prioritized roadmap while mentoring engineers and owning operational accountability for the team's pipelines.

Required Education & Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, a related technical field, or equivalent hands-on experience.
  • 8–12 years of experience in technology, with significant data-centric leadership.
  • 6–8 years hands-on experience architecting data solutions on a cloud platform.
  • 2+ years formally leading engineers or technical workstreams.

Preferred

  • Cloud Professional Data Engineer or ML Engineer certification.
  • Experience with healthcare data compliance frameworks (HIPAA, HL7, FHIR).
  • Experience setting standards for LLM/RAG data architecture at scale.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Expert-level SQL, data modeling, and semantic-layer design; sets standards for the team's schema/pipeline design patterns.
  • Sets the team's approach to batch/streaming architecture (Spark, Airflow, Databricks/Snowflake) and CI/CD practices.
  • Sets standards for the team's AI/RAG data pipelines (embedding strategy, vector-store selection, corpus curation) and AI-assisted development practices.
  • Directs and mentors a team of engineers; manages workload prioritization and on-time delivery.
  • Translates business ambiguity into actionable technical plans; regularly presents to stakeholders and audiences of 10+.
  • Coordinates handoffs with adjacent technical teams (data science, security, compliance) to ensure platform readiness.
  • Enforces security/privacy standards, including AI-specific risk considerations, across the team's work.

Job Functions

  • Lead and mentor a team/pod of engineers, prioritizing workload and driving on-time, Agile delivery.
  • Own source-management, version-control, and QA/testing standards for the team, including standards for AI-assisted code contributions.
  • Define and track the team's metrics strategy; own SLA/SLO tracking for pipelines and lead "back-to-green" plans when KPIs are missed.
  • Track, analyze, and report KPIs (pipeline uptime, MTTR, data-quality metrics) to leadership.
  • Own root-cause analysis and mitigation for complex pipeline/data-quality issues within the team's scope.
  • Serve as a primary technical liaison to business/clinical stakeholders, translating needs into the team's roadmap (pipelines, data products, AI/RAG capabilities).
  • Contribute cost/budget input for the team's cloud and AI/vector-database usage.
  • Own documentation, SOPs, and escalation pathways for the team.
  • Participate in and help coordinate the on-call rotation, owning escalation ownership when issues arise.

The compensation range for this position ranges from $165,830.00/year in our lowest geographic market up to 243,141.80 USD/year in our highest geographic market. jobs.excerpt: Ready to do the most impactful work of your career?
jobs.description:
Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? At Coinbase, we are uncompromising on our mission to increase economic freedom. The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn't a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits. If you're ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for "good enough," you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.” learn more about working at Coinbase.

As a Senior Software Engineer on the Data Platform team within the Platform group, you will help build the systems that centralize all of Coinbase's internal and third-party data. The Data Platform team makes it easy for teams across the company to access, process, and transform data for analytics, machine learning, and powering end-user experiences. You'll contribute to the full spectrum of our systems, from foundational data storage and processing to scalable pipelines, frameworks, and internal applications that make data efficiently available to every team at Coinbase.

What you'll do:

  • Own the design, development, and operation of foundational data services spanning cloud data warehouses, data lakes, orchestration (Airflow), batch processing (Spark, SQL), streaming (Kafka), query federation, and real-time event aggregation stores.
  • Build and maintain data integration and processing SDKs used by internal services and product teams throughout Coinbase to interact with the data platform reliably at scale.
  • Deliver self-service applications that empower users to manage, monitor, and troubleshoot their own data pipelines running on our platform infrastructure.
  • Architect end-to-end data security and observability services, including access controls across multiple storage and access layers, data quality tracking, dataset cataloging, lineage, and usage auditing.
  • Partner with data analysts, ML engineers, and security and compliance teams to convert functional requests into reusable, scalable patterns and assemble data microservices into platforms for critical business verticals.

Required Skills and Experience:

  • 5+ years of experience in backend software engineering, with hands-on experience building and operating data systems or data pipelines in production.
  • Proficiency in Python, Go, or Java for backend development, with demonstrated ability to build services that process and serve data at scale.
  • Experience with data infrastructure patterns including scale-out architectures, caching layers, key/value stores, and columnar storage systems.
  • Hands-on experience with SQL, Airflow, Spark, Kafka, or similar data processing and orchestration frameworks in production environments.
  • Experience with data security, access control, or data observability systems, including cataloging, lineage, or quality monitoring.
  • Utilizes generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality.

jobs.description:
Order.co is the System of Action for the Office of the CFO, transforming the way businesses purchase and pay into an intuitive, B2C-like shopping experience. Order.co leverages embedded AI agents and embedded financial products to reinvent the way businesses connect with their vendors.

End users enjoy a seamless, zero-training buying experience, while finance and procurement leaders gain a single platform to orchestrate how the business “should operate”. The result is an all-in-one solution that serves as a gravitational pull for spend and data, automating and eliminating procurement and finance workflows from requisition to reconciliation along the way.

Order.co is on the cutting edge of B2B Agentic Commerce, poised to be the market leader in creating a more predictive, prescriptive, and personalized experience for users.

Founded in 2016 and headquartered in New York City, Order.co oversees nearly half a billion in annualized spend across hundreds of customers like WeWork, SoulCycle, Lume, and [solidcore]. Order.co has raised $75M in funding from industry-leading investors like MIT, Stage 2 Capital, Rally Ventures, 645 Ventures, and more. Order.co has been proudly named a 50 to Watch by Spend Matters and a Best Place to Work by BuiltIn and Inc. Magazine.

The Role

As Director, Engineering Operations, you will build and run the operating system that helps

Product and Engineering translate strategy into measurable business and customer impact. You

will create clarity across outcomes, priorities, capacity, delivery health, risks, and decisions, then

turn that clarity into concise executive communication and disciplined organizational action. This

high-leverage leadership role partners closely with Product, Engineering, Data, Operations,

Finance, Go-to-Market, Customer Success, Security, and other business functions. You will play

a critical role in ensuring all functions are aligned and understand the expected outcomes.

Responsibilities

Executive Communication Impact

● Create a clear, executive-ready narrative connecting Product, Engineering, and Data

investments, delivery, and operational performance to customer and business outcomes

● Own recurring executive updates, company communications, and board-level inputs,

supported by a reliable source of truth for commitments, outcomes, and delivery health

● Surface material changes, trade-offs, risks, and decisions early, with concise context and

clear recommendations

Outcome & KPI Definition

● Translate company and product strategy into measurable outcomes, objectives, key

results, and operating KPIs with clear owners, baselines, targets, data sources, and

review cadences

● Develop a balanced view of customer and business impact, delivery effectiveness,

quality, reliability, security, efficiency, and organizational health

● Partner with Data, Finance, Product, and Engineering to improve instrumentation and

use KPI trends to guide decisions and evaluate results

Portfolio & Planning Cadence

● Design and operate annual, quarterly, and ongoing portfolio-planning cadences across

Product and Engineering

● Maintain a current portfolio view connecting strategic outcomes, initiatives, ownership,

dependencies, milestones, capacity, and risk

● Facilitate prioritization and sequencing decisions so assumptions, trade-offs, decision

rights, and changes are explicit

SDLC Process & Operating Reviews

● Define and continuously improve a lightweight, consistent software delivery lifecycle

from discovery through release, adoption, measurement, and learning

● Establish operating reviews focused on outcomes, delivery confidence, quality, reliability,

customer impact, constraints, risks, and decisions

● Use operating data, retrospectives, automation, and appropriately governed AI-enabled

practices to remove friction and improve delivery without adding unnecessary process

Resource & Capacity Planning

● Build a practical capacity model connecting portfolio demand with available teams,

Job Title: Senior Director, Patient Reported Outcomes

Job Location: Remote (US)

Job Location Type: Remote

Job Contract Type: Full-time

Job Seniority Level:

BeOne continues to grow at a rapid pace with challenging and exciting opportunities for experienced professionals. When considering candidates, we look for scientific and business professionals who are highly motivated, collaborative, and most importantly, share our passionate interest in fighting cancer.

General Description:


The Senior Director, Patient Reported Outcomes (PRO), is a senior scientific and strategic leader accountable for developing and executing integrated evidence-generation strategies that demonstrate the humanistic value of BeOne Medicines therapies. The role provides enterprise-level PRO leadership across one or more assets, indications, therapeutic areas, or regions and ensures that high-priority evidence needs are represented in integrated evidence plans, medical strategies, clinical development plans, and value and access strategies. The Senior Director influences portfolio and asset decisions, leads complex global humanistic programs, governs scientific quality and investment, and builds organizational capability through people leadership, matrix leadership, and external scientific engagement.


Working across Clinical Development, Medical Affairs, Global Value, Access and Pricing, Biostatistics, Data Science, Patient-Reported Outcomes, Regulatory, Safety, Publications, Legal, Compliance, Privacy, and regional teams, the incumbent translates evidence gaps into prioritized, feasible research programs. The role is accountable for strategic alignment, scientific rigor, compliant execution, timely delivery, budget stewardship, and effective communication of PRO evidence to internal decision-makers and appropriate external stakeholders.



Essential Functions of the Job:


Strategy and Portfolio Leadership

  • Own and provide senior leadership for global or regional PRO strategy across assigned assets, programs, therapeutic areas, or portfolios throughout the product lifecycle.
  • Shape integrated evidence plans by identifying, prioritizing, and revisiting evidence gaps in collaboration with cross-functional leadership and evidence-generating functions.
  • Ensure PRO perspectives are incorporated into asset strategy, clinical development plans, medical plans, lifecycle planning, launch preparation, reimbursement strategy, and annual operating and budget processes.
  • Advise senior leaders and governance bodies on PRO evidence priorities, investment trade-offs, methodological options, feasibility, timing, and risk.
  • Anticipate changes in healthcare systems, payer and health technology assessment expectations, data availability, methodological standards, and the competitive landscape, and translate those changes into strategic recommendations.

Scientific and Methodological Leadership

  • Provide executive scientific oversight for PRO real-world evidence, observational research, comparative effectiveness and safety research, burden-of-illness studies, patient preference research, health economic models, indirect treatment comparisons, evidence syntheses, and value communication deliverables.
  • Guide the selection and implementation of fit-for-purpose patient-reported outcome and other clinical outcome assessment strategies in partnership with PRO and Clinical Development experts.
  • Ensure research questions, protocols, analysis plans, models, and interpretations are scientifically rigorous, reproducible, transparent, and aligned with intended decision needs.
  • Provide senior review and approval, within delegated authority, of concepts, protocols, statistical analysis plans, technical reports, models, publications, and executive presentations.
  • Sponsor innovation in PRO, analytical, and data-science methods while ensuring appropriate validation, governance, and business relevance.

Program Governance and Execution

  • Lead a portfolio of complex, high-impact evidence-generation programs from concept through results dissemination and project closure.
  • Set priorities, decision rights, milestones, quality expectations, and escalation pathways for internal teams and external research partners.
  • Oversee project budgets, forecasts, contracts, vendor performance, timelines, risks, and resource allocation, and take timely corrective action when objectives are at risk.
  • Ensure appropriate cross-functional review and compliance with applicable legal, ethical, privacy, safety, regulatory, publication, data-governance, and company requirements.
  • Establish fit-for-purpose quality controls and independent technical review for complex analyses, models, and high-impact deliverables.
  • Ensure balanced interpretation of findings, including uncertainty, missingness, bias, confounding, generalizability, sensitivity analyses, and study limitations.

Cross-Functional and Executive Influence

  • Serve as the senior PRO partner to asset teams, medical and development leadership, access teams, governance committees, and regional stakeholders.
  • Build alignment across functions and geographies when priorities, evidence needs, timelines, or methodological perspectives differ.
  • Translate complex scientific and economic evidence into clear implications and recommendations for executive, clinical, payer, regulatory, and nontechnical audiences.
  • Facilitate timely decisions by framing options, trade-offs, dependencies, risks, and recommended actions.
  • Contribute to business development, due diligence, portfolio assessment, and external partnership evaluations, as assigned.
  • Lead or oversee publication and scientific communication strategies for assigned PRO programs in partnership with Publications and cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Represent BeOne Medicines at scientific congresses, professional associations, advisory forums, and other appropriate external engagements.
  • Build credible relationships with researchers, clinicians, payers, health economists, patient organizations, and other external experts in accordance with company policies.
  • Advance the company’s scientific reputation through high-quality research, peer-reviewed publications, presentations, and responsible methodological leadership.

People and Organizational Leadership

  • Lead, coach, and develop direct reports and provide matrix leadership to cross-functional colleagues, contractors, and external research teams.
  • Set clear objectives, provide actionable feedback, support development planning, and create an inclusive environment that promotes accountability, collaboration, and scientific challenge.
  • Assess capability and capacity needs and recommend hiring, external support, training, tools, standards, and operating-model improvements.
  • Promote consistent PRO practices, knowledge sharing, reusable resources, and continuous improvement across global and regional teams.
  • Demonstrate sound judgment, integrity, financial stewardship, and accountability for decisions and commitments.

Supervisory Responsibilities

  • Manages and develops one or more employees, as assigned, and provides senior functional direction to matrix teams, contractors, and external research partners.
  • Accountable for goal setting, performance and development discussions, workload prioritization, succession and capability planning, and a respectful, inclusive team environment.

Education Required:

  • Advanced degree in health economics, outcomes research, epidemiology, biostatistics, public health, psychometrics, pharmacy, medicine, or a related quantitative or clinical discipline, or equivalent education and relevant experience.

Required Qualifications:

  • Advanced Degree (Masters, PhD, PharmD, PhD, MD) with 10 or more years of progressively responsible experience in PRO, RWE, outcomes research, epidemiology, market access evidence, medical affairs, clinical research, or a related field, including substantial biopharmaceutical or healthcare-sector experience.
  • Demonstrated success defining and executing evidence strategies for complex assets, therapeutic areas, or portfolios in a global or multi-regional environment.
  • Deep expertise in several relevant methods, including observational study design, causal inference, comparative effectiveness, economic modeling, indirect treatment comparisons, evidence synthesis, PRO/COA methods, patient preference research, or analysis of claims, electronic health records, registries, or clinical-trial data.
  • Proven ability to influence senior leaders, governance bodies, and cross-functional teams without relying solely on formal authority.
  • Demonstrated leadership of complex programs, budgets, vendors, risks, competing priorities, people, and matrix teams.
  • Strong scientific communication record and excellent written, verbal, presentation, negotiation, and stakeholder-management skills.
  • Working knowledge of applicable research, privacy, safety, publication, compliance, and data-governance expectations.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Doctoral degree in a relevant discipline.
  • Significant oncology and hematology experience.
  • Experience with health technology assessment, reimbursement, regulatory, or value communication strategies across major global markets.
  • Demonstrated publication record and external scientific presence in PRO, epidemiology, health economics, or related methods.
  • Experience establishing functional standards, governance, centers of excellence, or enterprise-wide evidence-generation capabilities.
  • Experience with statistical or analytical software and critical review of code outputs, models, data specifications, tables, and figures.

Computer Skills:

  • PC, including MS Office Suite and MS Teams.
  • Proficiency with productivity, collaboration, presentation, project-management, and document-management platforms.
  • Familiarity with analytical tools, real-world data sources, economic-modeling applications, literature-review platforms, or regulated content systems is preferred.

Travel:

  • Approximately 25–30%, including domestic and international travel as business needs require.
  • Ability to participate in meetings across time zones and respond flexibly to critical business needs.
  • Ability to perform the essential functions of the role with or without reasonable accommodation.

Additional Position Information:

  • Reports to the Vice President, Integrative Evidence Generation and Health Economics, Global Medical Affairs.
  • Work location: Remote.
  • People-manager role with direct reports and/or matrix leadership, as assigned.

Global Competencies

When we exhibit our values of Patients First, Driving Excellence, Bold Ingenuity and Collaborative Spirit, through our twelve global competencies below, we help get more affordable medicines to more patients around the world.

  • Fosters Teamwork
  • Provides and Solicits Honest and Actionable Feedback
  • Self-Awareness
  • Acts Inclusively
  • Demonstrates Initiative
  • Entrepreneurial Mindset
  • Continuous Learning

jobs.description:
Product Strategy Analyst - New Customers (UK)

Hybrid in London, UK

We’re looking for a Product Strategy Analyst

You'll shape how new businesses become iwoca customers – the sign-up flow, the documents we ask for, and the models that decide who gets funded and on what terms.

The company

Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are.

That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed.

We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive.

The team

The New Customers team owns everything from a business's first application to a funded loan: the application flow, the logic that routes each application, the documents we ask customers for, and the models that set loan amounts and pricing.

The team is cross-functional – data scientists, analysts, and software engineers – and sets its own goals and direction. It partners closely with credit risk on the trade-offs behind every lending decision. Knowledge sharing is central to how the team works, supported by regular forums to share findings, and dedicated research and development time.

The role

As the Product Strategy Analyst, you'll run the projects that shape how new businesses join iwoca. You'll steer which experiments the team runs, weighing short-term gains against longer-term bets that compound over time, with customer lifetime value as your key metric.

  • Judgement and strategy. You'll set iwoca's new-customer lending strategy, weighing trade-offs between speed, friction, risk, and decision accuracy. You'll identify drop-off points and commercial opportunities across the conversion funnel, and propose the initiatives that address them.

  • Challenge and experimentation. You'll design, run, and interpret controlled experiments on changes to the customer journey and new loan features. You'll apply statistical thinking so decisions rest on evidence.

  • Autonomy and growth. You'll manage analytical and strategic projects end-to-end, sharing findings and recommendations directly with senior leadership. You'll partner with the Team Lead to shape the team's long-term roadmap, with the expectation of growing into a Team Lead role yourself.

The requirements

Essential:

  • Commercial analytics. You've worked in strategy, analytics, product, finance, or consulting. You understand how to use data to make commercial decisions on revenue, cost, or risk that the business acts on.

  • Quantitative foundations. You have a STEM background (degree or equivalent) in mathematics, statistics, physics, engineering, or similar. You reason about uncertainty and calibration, grounded in the underlying statistics.

  • First-principles thinking. You break complex problems into their core parts, decide which to tackle first, and iterate systematically to a solution.

  • Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail to your audience.

  • AI leverage. You've built AI workflows, or used AI to produce analysis or prototypes beyond what you could deliver alone. You judge when to use it and when not to.

Bonus:

  • Experimentation. You have designed, run, and interpreted controlled experiments, including A/B tests, to inform product or policy decisions.

  • Cross-functional delivery. You have worked closely with engineering or data science teams to get analytical insight into production systems.

  • Customer journey analytics. You have analysed and improved a customer journey, balancing conversion, risk, and long-term value.

  • Coding abilities. You can code for analysis, automation, or prototypes - whether directly or via AI coding tools like Claude Code.

The salary

We expect to pay from £60,000 to £80,000 for this role. But, we're open-minded, so definitely include your salary goals with your application. We routinely benchmark salaries against market rates, and run quarterly performance and salary reviews.

The culture

At iwoca, the best idea wins. We model our culture on independent thinking, challenging untested logic, and evidence-based decisions. We prioritise learning and growth, and give people the autonomy to develop in the direction that makes them most effective.

We're a tech company and believe in the power of AI to help us work faster and better. We provide the infrastructure where every iwocan always has access to the best models and where those models have access to all of our data. We will help our people to learn how to use and grow with the new tools available to them.

The offices

We put a lot of effort into making iwoca a great place to work:

  • Offices in London, Leeds, Berlin, and Frankfurt with plenty of drinks and snacks.

  • Events and community-led groups, including running groups, padel, and monthly ping-pong and pool competitions.

The benefits

  • Flexible working hours.

  • Medical insurance from Vitality, including discounted gym membership.

  • A private GP service (separate from Vitality) for you, your partner, and your dependents.

  • 25 days’ holiday per year, an extra day off for your birthday, the option to buy or sell an additional five days of annual leave, and unlimited unpaid leave.

  • A one-month, fully paid sabbatical after four years.

  • Instant access to external counselling and therapy sessions for team members that need emotional or mental health support.

  • 3% Pension contributions on total earnings.

  • An employee equity incentive scheme.

  • Generous parental leave and a nursery tax benefit scheme to help you save money.

  • Electric car scheme and cycle to work scheme.

  • Two company retreats a year: we’ve been to France, Italy, Spain, and further afield.

And to make sure we all keep learning, we offer:

  • A learning and development budget for everyone.

  • Company-wide talks with internal and external speakers.

  • Access to learning platforms like Treehouse.

Useful links:

  • iwoca benefits & policies

  • Interview welcome pack (TAP)

Compensation Range: £60K - £80K

jobs.excerpt: 🧠 About Legion HealthAt Legion Health, we believe everyone deserves fast, affordable, and world-class health care, and we’re developing the AI infrastructure to deliver it at scale.
jobs.description:
🧠 About Legion Health

At Legion Health, we believe everyone deserves fast, affordable, and world-class health care, and we’re developing the AI infrastructure to deliver it at scale.

Legion is building autonomous medical care, starting with psychiatry. Our AI-native care-delivery platform automates much of the administrative work required to deliver direct patient care, allowing clinicians and operations teams to focus on the moments where human judgment and attention matter most.

Our technical moat is hard to copy—we combine rich data, production AI, doctors in the loop, and end-to-end care operations to deliver measurably better care to a clinically complex patient population. This has helped us complete tens of thousands of visits in just two years while holding operations costs flat and achieving industry-leading patient NPS and retention.

While the last generation of healthcare startups made the existing system incrementally more efficient, Legion is rebuilding full-stack care delivery from first principles. Our vision is a 10X better patient experience that is higher quality, less expensive, and more scalable—and a 10X better clinician experience that frees providers to focus on what matters most: caring for patients.

Legion Health is backed by Y Combinator, leading venture capital firms, and founders from Function Health, Modern Health, Everly Health, Trusted Health, Clipboard Health, PatientPing, Sesame Care, Faire, EasyPost, and fuboTV.

Join us as we build the future of health care: faster, higher-quality, and more affordable, powered by clinicians, operators, and AI working together.

📍 Role Logistics

  • Job Type: Full-time contract

  • Role Type: Provider Operations / Recruiting Coordination / Onboarding / Payroll Support

  • Ideal Experience Level: 2+ years

  • Location: Fully remote

  • Work Hours: 9:00 AM–6:00 PM US Central Time

  • Hourly Compensation: $5–$15 per hour, based on experience

🚀 The Opportunity

Legion is hiring an exceptionally organized and detail-oriented Medical Virtual Assistant to help operate the systems that support our growing network of healthcare providers.

You will support providers throughout their relationship with Legion—from recruiting and onboarding through active operations, payroll preparation, and offboarding. Your work will help ensure candidates receive timely follow-up, new providers are ready to begin, operating records remain accurate, and payroll inputs are complete before they are finalized.

This is not a generic assistant role. You will own recurring, detail-heavy workflows that directly affect providers, internal teams, and Legion’s ability to deliver patient care. A missed document can delay a provider’s start date. An inaccurate status field can create confusion across teams. An overlooked payroll discrepancy can affect a provider’s pay. Precision and follow-through matter.

The right person enjoys bringing order to complex workflows. You should be comfortable maintaining spreadsheets and trackers, coordinating across multiple teams, following up persistently, documenting decisions, and identifying missing information before it becomes a larger problem.

This role is a strong fit for someone who enjoys checklists, healthcare operations, provider communication, reconciliation work, and continuously improving how recurring processes are run.

✅ Responsibilities and Deliverables

  • Coordinate provider recruiting operations, including:

    • Maintaining accurate candidate records and statuses.

    • Scheduling and confirming interviews.

    • Following up with candidates about outstanding steps.

    • Updating hiring records and internal trackers.

    • Coordinating handoffs between recruiting and onboarding.

  • Support provider onboarding from accepted offer through start readiness, including:

    • Collecting required documents and information.

    • Maintaining onboarding checklists and status trackers.

    • Following up promptly on missing or incomplete items.

    • Coordinating internal handoffs across relevant teams.

    • Confirming that required operational steps are complete before a provider begins.

    • Escalating blockers that could delay a provider’s start date.

  • Maintain accurate provider-operations records, including:

    • Provider rosters.

    • Recruiting and onboarding status.

    • Active, inactive, and offboarding providers.

    • State coverage and provider availability.

    • Collaborating-physician relationships.

    • Credentialing and payer-enrollment status.

    • Outstanding documents, approvals, and follow-up items.

  • Communicate clearly and professionally with providers through Slack, email, and approved internal systems.

  • Support weekly payroll preparation, including:

    • Gathering provider compensation inputs from approved systems.

    • Reviewing visit counts, no-shows, and late cancellations.

    • Updating payroll and payment trackers.

    • Reconciling discrepancies across source systems.

    • Confirming that supporting information is complete.

    • Escalating unresolved discrepancies before payroll is finalized.

    • Maintaining a clear record of changes, questions, and resolutions.

  • Coordinate across recruiting, credentialing, clinical operations, billing, finance, and payroll to keep provider workflows moving.

  • Maintain clear task queues and follow-up systems so that outstanding items do not fall through the cracks.

  • Document recurring workflows and update SOPs, checklists, and templates as processes evolve.

  • Identify opportunities to simplify, standardize, or automate repetitive administrative work.

  • Handle sensitive provider, company, hiring, and compensation information with discretion and care.

  • Raise unclear ownership, conflicting information, or potential errors promptly rather than making unsupported assumptions.

🏆 You’ll Be Successful If You…

  • Keep provider trackers accurate, current, and easy for other teams to understand.

  • Ensure candidates and providers receive timely, professional follow-up.

  • Help new providers complete onboarding requirements and become ready to start without preventable delays.

  • Catch missing information and payroll discrepancies before they create downstream problems.

  • Produce documentation that clearly explains what happened, what remains outstanding, and who owns the next step.

  • Manage recurring deadlines without needing repeated reminders.

  • Follow established procedures while noticing when a process is unclear, inefficient, or incomplete.

  • Move quickly without sacrificing accuracy.

  • Communicate professionally and confidently with clinicians, candidates, contractors, and internal teammates.

  • Remain calm and organized when priorities change or multiple deadlines overlap.

  • Build reusable checklists, trackers, and workflows that make provider operations easier to scale.

  • Earn the trust of providers and teammates through reliability, discretion, accuracy, and consistent follow-through.

🧰 Ideal Background and Skills

  • 2+ years of experience in one or more of the following:

    • Healthcare operations.

    • Provider operations.

    • Recruiting coordination.

    • Provider or employee onboarding.

    • Payroll or invoice support.

    • Human-resources administration.

    • Executive-assistant or virtual-operations support.

  • Strong preference for experience supporting:

    • Clinicians or other healthcare professionals.

    • Independent contractors.

    • Distributed or fully remote teams.

    • Recurring payroll, payment, or reconciliation workflows.

  • Excellent organizational skills and close attention to detail.

  • Strong spreadsheet skills, including maintaining structured trackers, reviewing data, reconciling differences, and identifying missing information.

  • Careful with names, dates, pay periods, visit counts, status fields, and supporting documentation.

  • Clear, concise, and professional written English.

  • Comfortable following up persistently and respectfully with providers and internal teammates.

  • Able to manage several recurring workflows and deadlines simultaneously.

  • Proactive about identifying blockers, discrepancies, unclear ownership, and overdue action items.

  • Comfortable working in a fast-moving startup where processes may evolve as the company grows.

  • Able to handle confidential provider, recruiting, company, and compensation information appropriately.

  • Familiarity with HIPAA-sensitive healthcare environments and appropriate information-handling practices.

  • Experience with any of the following is a plus:

    • Google Sheets.

    • Slack.

    • Ashby or another applicant-tracking system.

    • Healthie or another EHR or practice-management platform.

    • Looker Studio or similar reporting tools.

    • Stripe or contractor-payment platforms.

    • Payroll, invoicing, or payment-reconciliation workflows.

    • Telehealth or behavioral-health operations.

    • Credentialing and payer enrollment.

    • Healthcare billing.

    • Provider scheduling or workforce operations.

⚠️ This Role Is Not a Fit If You…

  • Prefer exclusively patient-facing work and do not enjoy internal operations.

  • Dislike spreadsheets, trackers, checklists, or reconciliation work.

  • Need every day to follow exactly the same workflow.

  • Wait for repeated instructions instead of proactively following up on outstanding work.

  • Are uncomfortable asking questions or escalating conflicting information.

  • Are casual about deadlines, documentation, confidentiality, or payroll accuracy.

  • Frequently lose track of details when managing several workflows at once.

  • Prefer completing individual tasks without taking ownership of the full outcome.

💰 Compensation & Role Benefits

  • Hourly Compensation: $5–$15 per hour, based on experience.

  • Job Type: Full-time contract.

  • Schedule: 9:00 AM–6:00 PM US Central Time.

  • Work Setup: Fully remote.

  • Impact: Build the provider-operations foundation that enables clinicians to spend more time caring for patients.

  • Autonomy and Learning: Develop experience across recruiting coordination, provider onboarding, healthcare operations, payroll preparation, and process improvement.

  • Growth Opportunities: Take on broader ownership across provider operations, onboarding, recruiting coordination, payroll operations, quality assurance, or team leadership as Legion grows.

🤝 Equal Employment Opportunity

We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees, contractors, and applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic under applicable law. We encourage applicants from all backgrounds to apply.

jobs.description:
Order.co is the System of Action for the Office of the CFO, transforming the way businesses purchase and pay into an intuitive, B2C-like shopping experience. Order.co leverages embedded AI agents and embedded financial products to reinvent the way businesses connect with their vendors.

End users enjoy a seamless, zero-training buying experience, while finance and procurement leaders gain a single platform to orchestrate how the business “should operate”. The result is an all-in-one solution that serves as a gravitational pull for spend and data, automating and eliminating procurement and finance workflows from requisition to reconciliation along the way.

Order.co is on the cutting edge of B2B Agentic Commerce, poised to be the market leader in creating a more predictive, prescriptive, and personalized experience for users.

Founded in 2016 and headquartered in New York City, Order.co oversees nearly half a billion in annualized spend across hundreds of customers like WeWork, SoulCycle, Lume, and [solidcore]. Order.co has raised $75M in funding from industry-leading investors like MIT, Stage 2 Capital, Rally Ventures, 645 Ventures, and more. Order.co has been proudly named a 50 to Watch by Spend Matters and a Best Place to Work by BuiltIn and Inc. Magazine.

Role summary

We are hiring a Principal Applied AI Architect to set how data and intelligence work at Order.co: the target-state architecture, the standards that keep it coherent, and the company-level bets that turn proprietary procurement data into durable advantage. This is a senior individual contributor role. You will identify company-level objectives, make the business case to fund them, and land production systems that move primary company KPIs.

You will be the Head of Data's closest technical partner: the complementary technical leader to a strategy, product, and business lens. You keep those bets grounded in what we can actually do with the systems we have, and you are the person who knows what it would take to change that.

You sit on the data team. Applied AI Scientists take the architecture into product initiatives and own the science through to the metric. Senior AI / Data Engineers take the same architecture into the platform and own the production path. You are the person who holds those two paths on one spine, and who can still get on the keyboard when the first systems need to exist.

The work is architecture-first, with a real engineering bar. You will be fluent across stacks, treat security, reliability, and maintainability as delivery criteria rather than afterthoughts, and set a production quality standard that other teams can reuse. You will also stay a working applied scientist: statistical depth, model and agent judgment, and the ability to go from a strategic imperative to a shipped system. This is not an academic role. Understanding production systems and the business they serve is required, and you will get a change through operations and the other stakeholders who gate a real deploy.

How we think about the work

Great product capabilities stay modular when they share one canonical picture of the business: catalog, mapping, pricing, availability, and vendor truth. That picture has to be accurate first. Then it has to move: scalable pipelines and serving paths so the same data can feed the business and product independently of where they may sit. Intelligence, both deterministic and learned, is what we build on top of that advantage. The quality of the intelligence is bounded by the quality and availability of the data underneath it.

Your job is to make that stack a company strategy, not a collection of projects. Accuracy funds the platform. The platform funds intelligence. Intelligence that cannot name the data it depends on is not a bet we take.

What you will own

Company architecture for data and intelligence

You will define the target-state architecture for the data estate and for applied AI, aligned to business priorities rather than tooling fashion. That includes how warehouse and lake, pipelines, streaming, and integrations fit together, and how model serving, retrieval, embeddings, prompt and model management, guardrails, and evaluation fit on top of that same governed foundation. You will establish source-of-truth models and a shared semantic picture of the business so fragmented sources converge into one reliable platform, which is the foundation AI depends on.

You will set naming, modeling, lineage, and integration standards, and you will be the review that keeps new designs on that spine. You will make security, privacy, and compliance part of the design: classification, handling of sensitive data, access control, retention, and audit through every layer. Cost, performance, and reliability are first-class constraints in the architecture you defend, not optimizations someone else discovers later.

AI strategy, standards, and the investment case

You will own where AI creates durable advantages for the data function, including build versus buy, what we sequence, and what we deliberately skip. You will make AI demand a funded platform modernization story: the data, contracts, features, and retrieval infrastructure the work requires, sized in impact, cost, risk, and return, so leadership can actually fund it. You will set institutional standards for evaluation, rollout, monitoring, model risk, and responsible AI so that no output, human or AI, ships on trust alone.

You will advise the Head of Data, and product and engineering leadership, on what the current stack can support, what it cannot, what it costs, and what it is likely to return, before the bet is made. You will set technical direction for the AI portfolio across initiatives. You will track the frontier without chasing it: pilot what matters, kill what does not, and convert the rest into production at company scale.

Delivery at company altitude

You will turn strategy into actionable projects, contribute to quarterly planning, and keep stakeholders in the loop as you remove blockers. You will direct a mix of human and agentic workstreams, accountable for the output of both. You will still execute: roughly half the time is implementation, because architecture that you cannot land is a slide. That includes passing the same production gates as everyone else. Operations, security, and the people who have to live with what you ship are not a handoff at the end. They are how the work gets into production.

You will mentor Applied AI Scientists and other individual contributors, and you will set the coherence standard (domain model, patterns, decision records) so someone, or an agent, can pick up work cold and land it right. You will raise the production engineering bar in AI systems across teams: observability, resilience, and the operational loop that makes a launch survivable.

What we are working on now

  • Accuracy at Scale. Make location, price, availability, and lead time trustworthy enough that buyers and product can act on them. The architecture, contracts, and quality bar that keep a single source of truth as we grow.
  • Adaptive Procurement. Use that same foundation to change how customers plan and place orders, including predictive timing inside real procurement constraints: org structure, budgets, approved catalogs, and vendor contracts.
  • The intelligence layer on that spine, including predictive ordering and agentic copilots in core workflows, with evaluation and operations underneath so we can tell a model that looks good offline from a capability that moves the business.

What we are looking for

  • At least 14 years in applied data science, machine learning, data architecture, or production AI systems, with a track record of landing work that moved a company-level metric you can name.
  • Experience as the technical counterpart to a product, strategy, or business leader, where your job was to ground the roadmap in what the systems could actually do.
  • Deep working knowledge of production systems and of the business they serve. That is required, not a plus. Research depth without a deploy record is not the profile.
  • Ownership of target-state architecture across data and applied AI, not models or pipelines in isolation: you have set the spine, the standards, and the review, and you have partnered with engineering to land it.
  • Repeated delivery of production systems you personally designed, defended, and got through operational and stakeholder gates to production, including serving, retrieval, evaluation, guardrails, and the operational loop around them.
  • The ability to size an initiative (direct and indirect impact, cost, risk, and return) and turn that into a business case leadership actually funded.
  • Real depth in current large language model and agent technology, meaning you know where it works, how it fails, how you evaluate it, and when a simpler deterministic approach is the better answer, plus a strong quantitative foundation in experimentation, statistical reasoning, and causal thinking.
  • Fluency across stacks and a production engineering bar: infrastructure as code, CI/CD, observability, and security and reliability treated as delivery criteria. You can work with warehouse, lake, and cloud data platforms as production software even when you are not the person on call for every pipeline.
  • Heavy daily use of AI-native engineering workflows across design, coding, debugging, and review for at least the past 18 months, along with the judgment to know where to verify and what not to trust.
  • Working implementation proficiency across at least two cloud or technical ecosystems, for example AWS and GCP.
  • Evidence that you have mentored senior individual contributors and set standards other teams reused, and that you can align executives and technical leaders when the situation is ambiguous.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience with retrieval systems, vector search, ranking, recommendation, or production personalization.
  • Experience designing source-of-truth models, semantic layers, or master and reference data that multiple product surfaces actually consumed.
  • Experience setting model governance, monitoring, and responsible AI standards for an organization rather than a single initiative.
  • Experience in e-commerce, B2B procurement, vendor management, financial products, or heavy integration with external systems.
  • An advanced degree in a quantitative field is welcome; it is not a requirement. We care that you have shipped.

What success looks like in the first 6 to 9 months

  • The Head of Data is planning against a sequenced view of the data and AI portfolio that you own together, with at least one company-level bet in motion and a sized impact story behind it.
  • Target-state architecture and standards are in use: new data and AI designs go through a coherent review instead of accumulating as one-off systems.
  • Applied AI Scientists and Senior AI / Data Engineers are working from the same spine, so intelligence lands on governed infrastructure rather than beside it.
  • Evaluation, monitoring, and responsible-AI controls are the default on production AI, not a special project.
  • You have shipped something yourself, through the operational and stakeholder gates that make a deploy real. Architecture without a production artifact in this window is not the job.

Working model

You sit on the data team as the Head of Data's closest technical partner, and you are hands-on from day one. You will partner with Product, Engineering, Operations, our Applied AI Scientists, and our Senior AI / Data Engineers. We ship iteratively and we judge work by the company outcome it produces. This role is remote within the United States.

Interview process

The process begins with a conversation with our recruiter, followed by a conversation with our Head of Data, who is the hiring manager for this role. If we both want to continue, we will send you a short written exercise on a real problem from our stack, designed to take about 90 minutes, and that exercise becomes the basis for a 60-minute working session with two of our senior engineers from platform and data engineering. From there you will speak with a senior business executive, our VP of Engineering, and our CTO, and we close with a values conversation with our People Ops team. That is seven conversations plus the written exercise, and your recruiter will keep you informed at each step.

What You'll Receive

  • Competitive compensation package
  • Employer-sponsored 401(k) with match
  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • Flexible time off and hybrid work environment
  • The anticipated annual salary range for this role is $225,000 - $275,000. Actual compensation and title will be commensurate with experience, qualifications, knowledge, and skills.

jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer
jobs.excerpt: About Fòs FeministaFòs Feminista is a global intersectional feminist organization advancing the sexual and reproductive health and rights of women, girls, and gender-diverse people.
jobs.description:
About Fòs Feminista

Fòs Feminista is a global intersectional feminist organization advancing the sexual and reproductive health and rights of women, girls, and gender-diverse people. Led and governed by the Global South, Fòs Feminista works through a constellation of affiliated organizations, legal entities, strategic partnerships, and movement relationships with around 200 civil society partners across 40 countries.

Our work integrates advocacy, grantmaking, research, movement-building, sexual and reproductive healthcare, and innovative finance to strengthen feminist organizations and movements worldwide. Operating across multiple jurisdictions and institutional structures, Fòs Feminista brings together legal, political, philanthropic, and movement strategies to advance gender justice and achieve lasting systemic change.

Position overview

Fòs Feminista is seeking a Chief Operating Officer to provide strategic and operational leadership across the organization.
Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer and serving on the Strategic Management Team (SMT), the COO will translate strategy into coordinated plans, sound resource decisions, effective institutional systems, and accountable implementation.
The COO will integrate People, Inclusion, and Culture; Business Intelligence, Evaluation and Research; and Legal Affairs. The Chief Financial Officer will report to the COO for operational integration and fiduciary responsibilities while retaining a direct relationship with the CEO. The role requires a leader who can move between strategy and execution and work across functions, regions, and cultures.

Position within the organization

Reports to: Chief Executive Officer

Leadership body: Strategic Management Team

Direct and functional oversight:

• People, Inclusion, and Culture

  • Business Intelligence, Evaluation and Research
    • Legal Affairs
    • Chief Financial Officer, within the dual-reporting arrangement described above

Principal responsibilities

1. Executive leadership and strategic execution
• Serve as a strategic partner to the CEO and an active member of the SMT, contributing to the development, review, and implementation of organizational strategy.
• Translate priorities into annual and multi-year plans that connect responsibilities, timelines, resources, and measures of progress.
• Help SMT assess opportunities and challenges in relation to mission impact, finances, organizational capacity, risk, and effects on partners; monitor progress and address barriers.
• Support organizational continuity, assume responsibilities delegated by the CEO, and represent Fòs Feminista with the Board, partners, donors, advisers, and other external actors as appropriate.

2. Organizational integration and performance
• Act as a principal integrator across strategy, finance, people, evidence, legal affairs, resource mobilization, and operational capacity.
• Strengthen cross-unit planning, clarify responsibilities and decision points, and ensure that organizational gaps and matters without a clear institutional owner are addressed.
• Lead policy development, integrated systems implementation, the responsible use of AI, and major organizational change to improve efficiency and cost-effectiveness.

3. Financial stewardship and organizational sustainability
• Provide executive oversight of financial planning and performance with the CFO and CEO, connecting budgets, forecasts, staffing, fundraising projections, program commitments, and organizational priorities.
• Support budgets, financial scenarios, and resource-allocation recommendations; monitor performance, sustainability, and risks; and ensure that SMT receives timely analysis.
• Ensure strong systems for financial controls, restricted funding, grants and contracts, audits, procurement, and compliance while protecting the CFO’s professional and fiduciary responsibilities, including direct access to the CEO and, where appropriate, the Board.

4. Connection with resource mobilization

  • Align revenue strategies and major proposals with organizational priorities, delivery capacity, financial forecasts, commitments to partners, realistic costing, and risk analysis.
    • Strengthen coordination throughout the funding cycle; support governance and performance monitoring of the Feminist Impact Fund; and assess the funding portfolio’s effect on longer-term sustainability.
    • Join selected donor discussions when institutional, financial, or operational questions require executive participation. Fundraising strategy, donor cultivation, and revenue generation remain with Resource Mobilization and the CEO.

5. People, inclusion, and culture

  • Provide strategic leadership to People, Inclusion, and Culture and ensure that recruitment, performance, compensation, development, succession, and staff well-being support the mission and strategy.
    • Strengthen management practice, organizational design, workforce planning, accountability, and team development while sustaining trust and collaboration.
    • Ensure that people practices reflect feminist values, equity and inclusion, and a distributed multilingual workforce, and that difficult matters can be addressed with clarity, fairness, and appropriate confidentiality.

6. Business intelligence, evidence, and organizational learning
• Provide strategic oversight to Business Intelligence, Evaluation and Research; strengthen the use of data in planning and decisions; and ensure that reporting and indicators serve learning and accountability.
• Ensure appropriate governance, protection, and ethical use of organizational and partner data. Oversee and integrate staff safety, digital and information security, AI risks, and crisis response.

7. Legal affairs, compliance, and risk

  • Provide executive oversight of Legal Affairs and ensure that legal considerations enter organizational planning and decisions early.
    • Maintain an organization-wide approach to legal, financial, operational, safeguarding, security, data, reputational, and people-related risks, including appropriate controls, escalation, continuity arrangements, and responses to significant compliance matters.
    • Ensure that contractual, regulatory, and governance obligations across jurisdictions are understood and managed.
    • Protect the professional independence of Legal Affairs. Its head retains direct access to the CEO and, when required, the appropriate Board body, including for concerns involving any senior manager or the COO.

Decision-making and authority

The COO will exercise authority delegated by the CEO and established through organizational policies, approved plans, and governance responsibilities. Decisions with significant strategic, financial, legal, reputational, workforce, or partner implications will be brought to the CEO, SMT, or Board. The COO will support them with integrated analysis, clear options, and effective implementation.

Leadership profile

The successful candidate will be a senior organizational leader with the judgment, experience, and relational capacity to work across multiple functions and institutional contexts. They will combine strategic perspective with disciplined execution and lead through coordination, trust, and influence as well as formal reporting relationships.

They will bring:

  • Demonstrated experience in a senior executive or enterprise-wide role in a complex international nonprofit, philanthropic, social-impact, or other mission-driven organization.
    • Experience leading or integrating several functions, such as finance, people and culture, operations, legal or compliance, organizational data, strategy implementation, or business development.
    • Strong financial literacy and experience using budgets, forecasts, and analysis to guide decisions and connect strategy with measurable results.
    • Experience working across countries, cultures, legal environments, or distributed teams and building productive relationships with senior colleagues, boards, staff, partners, donors, and advisers.
    • Experience leading change, strengthening systems without unnecessary bureaucracy, supporting functional leaders, and fostering collective accountability, with excellent judgment in sensitive matters.
    • A clear commitment to feminist principles, sexual and reproductive health and rights, racial and gender justice, and leadership from the Global South.
    • An understanding of partnership-based organizations and systems responsive to partner priorities. Professional fluency in English is required; Spanish, Portuguese, or French is an asset.

No single professional pathway is required. Candidates may come from operations, finance, organizational strategy, people and culture, international nonprofit management, philanthropy, social enterprise, or another relevant field, provided they demonstrate the breadth required for enterprise-level leadership.

Personal and leadership qualities

The COO should be:

  • Strategically minded and attentive to implementation, able to move between organizational detail and long-term questions and create clarity in ambiguous situations.
    • Collaborative but prepared to make difficult decisions, hold colleagues accountable, respect their expertise, and listen across differences.
    • Transparent, reliable, calm under pressure, and committed to shared leadership, sound delegation, and collective governance.

Indicators of success

During the initial period, success in the role would include:

  • Clearer integration among Finance; People, Inclusion, and Culture; Business Intelligence; Legal Affairs; Resource Mobilization; and other units.
    • Greater consistency among strategy, budgets, staffing, fundraising commitments, operational capacity, and organizational evidence.
    • Clear and trusted planning, follow-through, decision-making, and escalation processes, with stronger support for managers.
    • Effective management of institutional risk through systems that remain proportionate and responsive to partners.
    • A trusted working relationship among the CEO, COO, CFO, SMT, and Board, and a leadership culture combining accountability with feminist values.

Location: This position is fully remote.

Compensation: Fòs Feminista offers generous compensation consistent with competitive salaries and a benefits package that includes private health coverage, life insurance, retirement benefits, paid sick, vacation leave and parental leave, holidays, and flexible working arrangements. The annual salary is up to USD up to $220,000.

Safeguarding Commitments
Fòs Feminista is committed to ensuring that the health, rights and wellbeing of all children, young people, and vulnerable populations who work and engage with Fòs Feminista ’s Team Members and Associated Persons are respected and protected in their interactions with them and requires all its Team Members and Associated Persons to share this commitment.

The successful candidate must:
• Demonstrate an understanding of and commitment to safeguarding in the United States and the international context.
• Sign and adhere to Fòs Feminista’s International Safeguarding Policy and Safeguarding Code of Conduct, including the minimum operating standards for protection from sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA).

Equal Opportunity Employer Statement
Fòs Feminista is an equal opportunity employer dedicated to advancing sexual and reproductive rights and health and dismantling inequities from a feminist intersectional lens. Reproductive justice, racial justice, and diversity are driving forces for us.
Fòs Feminista provides equal opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to age, race, color, disability, national origin, religion, creed, gender, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital and partnership status, genetic information, veteran status or any other protected category under federal, state and local law.
At Fòs Feminista, we continue to build an inclusive culture that encourages, supports, and celebrates the diverse voices and experiences of our employees. We strongly encourage applications from all kinds of backgrounds to build a diverse workforce in which all social and minority groups are represented.

  • Excellent written and spoken English, with the presence to lead conversations with founders and C-level decision-makers
  • Organised and self-directed, able to manage multiple deals and partner relationships at once

About Augment

Augment is making private markets simple. We're a FINRA-registered marketplace where accredited investors can buy and sell shares in top pre-IPO companies, and where shareholders can get real liquidity before a public offering.
