Job Summary:

First Due is the leading cloud-native software platform for fire and EMS agencies in the United States. More than 3,000 agencies and 500,000 first responders rely on First Due every day for incident reporting, pre-incident planning, ePCR, scheduling, fire prevention, mobile response, training, and AI-powered analytics. We are FedRAMP High certified, power 42% of all national NERIS submissions, and count FDNY among our flagship customers.

Our Customer Support function is undergoing a major transformation. We are building a professionally scaled, data-driven organization with real infrastructure, real process discipline, and real career paths. This role is a critical part of that build.

We are looking for someone who has done this work before. Not at the strategic level. At the ground level. You have run a support queue, coached agents through hard tickets, built a QA program that changed behavior, and used data to figure out why the queue was growing before someone had to tell you. You have been the person in the room who knows how the operation actually works because you built the processes your team runs on.

This is not a maintenance role. We are building, and we need someone who knows what good looks like because they have built it themselves.

Key Responsibilities:

This role owns the daily execution and operational health of a support team, reporting to the Senior Director, Customer Support. You will directly manage team leads and individual contributors, and you will be accountable for the performance, development, and output of your team against defined standards and KPIs.

Daily Operations and Queue Management

  • Own the daily health of the support queue. Monitor ticket volume, aging, backlog growth, and routing accuracy. When something is off, you see it before anyone has to flag it.
  • Ensure tickets are triaged correctly, assigned to the right agents, and worked to resolution within SLA targets. Enforce status discipline so the queue reflects reality, not aspiration.
  • Manage escalations within the team. Know when a ticket needs to move up, when it needs a different skill set, and when an agent is stuck and needs coaching rather than reassignment.
  • Run daily and weekly operational cadences: queue reviews, stand-ups, ticket audits, and backlog scrubs. These are not optional when they get busy. They are most important when they get busy.
  • Act as a hands-on escalation point for complex or sensitive customer issues that exceed frontline capability.

Team Performance and Coaching

  • Directly manage a team of support agents and team leads. Set clear expectations, deliver regular feedback, and hold the team accountable to defined performance standards.
  • Own the QA and coaching cycle for your team. Review tickets regularly, identify patterns in agent performance, and run structured coaching sessions that connect feedback to specific behaviors.
  • Track individual and team-level KPIs: CSAT, first response time, time to resolution, first contact resolution, ticket volume per agent, and quality scores. Use the data to drive coaching, not just reporting.
  • Conduct regular 1:1s with every direct report. These are working sessions, not status meetings. The goal is development, unblocking, and honest feedback in both directions.
  • Identify performance gaps early and address them directly. Build and execute performance improvement plans when necessary, with clear timelines and measurable criteria.

People Development and Team Health

  • Own onboarding for new support team members. Build and maintain a structured ramp program that gets agents to competence on a defined timeline, not whenever it happens to click.
  • Develop and maintain training materials, knowledge resources, and competency benchmarks for your team. When the product changes or a new module launches, your team is prepared before the tickets arrive.
  • Identify high-potential individuals and invest in their development. Create visibility into what the next step looks like and what it takes to get there.
  • Monitor team morale and workload distribution. Burnout is a leading indicator, not a trailing one. You are close enough to the team to see it early and act on it.
  • Foster a culture of ownership and curiosity. The best support agents do not just close tickets. They understand why the ticket exists and whether it should exist at all.

Process Execution and Improvement

  • Execute the support processes and standards defined by the Director. When a process is not working on the ground, surface it with data and a recommendation, not just a complaint.
  • Maintain and enforce ticket classification discipline: module tagging, ticket type, priority, and status accuracy. Clean data starts with consistent agent behavior, and consistent agent behavior starts with management reinforcement.
  • Identify recurring ticket patterns and escalation drivers within your team. Document them, quantify them, and bring them to leadership with enough context to act on.
  • Contribute to process design and improvement initiatives. You are closest to how the work actually gets done, and your input is expected, not optional.
  • Ensure that escalations leaving your team for Product or Engineering are well-documented, properly categorized, and include everything the receiving team needs to act without a follow-up conversation.

Reporting and Visibility

  • Deliver weekly team performance reports that are accurate, on time, and actionable. Your Director should never have to ask you how your team is doing.
  • Maintain clean, current data in the support platform. Ticket fields are filled correctly, statuses reflect actual state, and your team understands that data hygiene is part of the job, not extra work.
  • Surface risks, blockers, and capacity concerns proactively. If the queue is growing, if a product release is generating unexpected volume, or if you are losing coverage, raise it before it becomes a crisis.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Work with peer managers across Support, Customer Success, and Services to coordinate on shared customers, handoff points, and escalation paths.
  • Partner with Product and Engineering contacts on escalated issues. Represent the customer problem clearly and follow through on resolution timelines.
  • Participate in product release readiness activities. Review release notes, identify likely support impact, and prepare your team for what is coming.

Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of experience in customer support operations, with at least 2 years directly managing a team of 8+ support agents or specialists in a B2B SaaS environment.
  • You have built or substantially improved a support operation. You did not inherit a well-running machine. You built the processes, set the standards, and developed the team that runs on them.
  • Hands-on experience running a support queue: you have personally triaged tickets, coached agents through complex issues, and managed a backlog under pressure. You know what the work feels like, not just what the metrics say.
  • Experience designing and running QA and coaching programs that changed agent behavior. You can point to specific examples where your coaching moved a metric, not just checked a box.
  • Operational fluency with a modern support platform (Zendesk strongly preferred). You understand views, triggers, automations, macros, and reporting well enough to manage through the tool, not around it.
  • Experience tracking and reporting on support KPIs (CSAT, FRT, TTR, FCR, ticket volume, quality scores). You have built or maintained a team scorecard and used it to drive decisions.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills. You can write a clear process document, deliver direct feedback in a 1:1, and present your team's performance to leadership without sugarcoating.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in mission-critical, compliance-sensitive, or government-adjacent B2B SaaS environments. Public safety, healthcare, infrastructure, or similar industries where errors have real-world consequences.
  • Experience managing distributed or remote teams across multiple time zones.
  • Familiarity with Jira or similar tools for tracking escalations to Product and Engineering teams.

Marsello helps retailers know their customers and keep them coming back. We're at a genuine turning point — and we're looking for a Head of Loyalty to lead it.

Brand & market position. You'll lead Marsello's efforts to demonstrate its value — defining who we're for, what we believe about loyalty, and making sure that point of view shows up consistently across our website, product, sales and customer success. Lead volume and pipeline from our own channels sit with you.

Product direction. You'll set the vision for a new loyalty marketing product, built on proven loyalty principles from day one — translating enterprise-grade sophistication into simple, opinionated tools that small and medium-sized businesses can actually run. You'll work closely with our Product team to bring it to life and turn it into a genuine growth engine.

A team you'll build up. Six direct reports across Product and Marketing, unified under one loyalty mandate. You'll set the standard, the direction and the coaching that lets them do their best work.

A voice that carries. As Marsello's internal authority on loyalty marketing, you'll shape how the whole business — Product, Marketing, Customer Success, Sales — thinks about building customer loyalty, and you'll represent us externally with customers, partners and the wider loyalty community.

Why Marsello

jobs.description:
As the DEV Community Manager, you'll be the day-to-day steward of the DEV () community. You'll spend your time on the platform, get to know its most engaged members, keep the experience welcoming and high quality, and make sure people get fast, thoughtful help when they need it.

This role is for a DEV power user who wants to make it their job. You'll represent the community's needs inside MLH, bring strong judgment to content and engagement, build connections between the MLH and DEV communities, and help DEV keep being a place developers want to show up.

What You’ll Do

  • Live on DEV: Be active on the platform every day - reading, commenting, reacting, and posting, and build a deep understanding of how it works, its culture, and its most engaged members.

  • Moderation: Own moderation on DEV, setting the standard for what belongs on the platform and making the final call on tough cases. Recruit, support, and work alongside our volunteer moderators to keep the community safe, welcoming, and high quality.

  • Community Support: Monitor and manage community support channels and inboxes so members get prompt, thoughtful responses.

  • Listen and Route: Spot influential contributors, recurring concerns, and emerging community issues. Route feedback, bug reports, feature requests, and escalations to the right internal teams.

  • Source New Contributors: Work with popular and prolific technical writers from across the developer ecosystem to bring their insights to the DEV platform.

  • Monitor External Community Platforms: Oversee or support our presence on Reddit and other relevant channels.

  • Content Curation: Curate the best of the community through editorial roundups, newsletters, and email marketing.

  • Editorial Judgment: Recognize valuable contributions, elevate quality content, and keep a consistent brand tone and voice.

  • AI-Assisted Work: Use AI tools to speed up community and content work, and apply your own taste, context, and quality control to the final output.

Benefits

  • Competitive salary (range is posted above)

  • Stock options

  • Medical, dental, vision benefits and 401K

  • Unlimited PTO

  • Travel opportunities

About MLH

Major League Hacking's (MLH) mission is to empower hackers. Each year over 100,000 young technologists and innovators around the world attend MLH events and join our community. Our events provide a self-driven environment where community members learn from each other outside the confines of traditional academia. The MLH team grew out of this movement and is dedicated to making it accessible to the entire world.

Earlier this year, we acquired DEV (dev.to), an online community for software developers. Our combined ecosystem now supports millions of creators at every stage of their journey.

  • We’re a team of 20 full-time people primarily based on the US East Coast (mostly NYC) with team members in Louisville, London, and India, to name a few.

  • Our co-founders, Swift and Jon, were recognized for their work in education by Forbes in the 2017 30 Under 30 list.

  • We work with some of the top technology brands like Google Gemini, ElevenLabs, Cloudflare, and more, to help them reach our community and get the latest and greatest tools into their hands.

  • We have a group of world-class investors including General Catalyst, Alexis Ohanian (Reddit), Jeff Lawson (Twilio), and Sundance DiGiovanni (Major League Gaming).

  • We are a mission driven B Corp, committed to responsibly serving the world and our community.

Requirements

Who You Are

  • Active in the DEV Community:You're an active, established member of DEV, with a history of contributing to and engaging on the platform. You understand DEV's culture, its members, and what makes community content feel authentic. A DEV profile with established history is required for this role.

  • A Discord Operator: You've gone beyond participating in Discord communities. You've moderated, set up bots, built automations, or helped run a server.

  • Comfortable Across Community Platforms: You know your way around Reddit and other online communities.

  • A Clear, Polished Writer You write and edit well, and you have strong instincts for curating content.

  • GitHub-Literate: You understand the lifecycle of a community-reported issue, from report to fix.

  • Level-Headed in Gray Areas:You make good calls in ambiguous situations, like moderation decisions, content concerns, and support escalations.

  • AI Fluent: You use AI tools as a starting point, then improve, curate, and adapt what they produce.

Please note: This role works closely with team members in and around New York, but we’re open to candidates in any location. You’ll need at least four hours of overlap with US Eastern Time each workday. If that works for you and you’re excited about the role, we’d love to see your application!

Job Summary

The Denials/Billing Coordinator ensures the accuracy, compliance, and performance of revenue cycle operations across behavioral health and substance use disorder services. This role resolves claim denials, improves billing processes, and drives accurate, compliant reimbursement across payers.

Partnering across clinical, coding, and billing teams, the Analyst ensures documentation integrity, identifies trends, reduces revenue leakage, and supports consistent, audit-ready practices using tools including the Credible EHR.

Job Summary

The Denials Coordinator is responsible for managing, investigating, and resolving insurance claim denials to support accurate and timely reimbursement. This position serves as the central point of coordination for denial tracking, appeals management, root cause analysis, and payer follow-up. The Denials Coordinator partners with Revenue Cycle, Clinical, Billing, Coding, and Authorization teams to reduce avoidable denials, improve reimbursement outcomes, and support operational excellence across Minnesota Adult & Teen Challenge.

Essential Job Responsibilities:

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential job duty satisfactorily. The essential functions include the following:

  • Manage insurance claim denials from identification through final resolution.
  • Review explanation of benefits (EOBs), remittance advice, and payer communications to determine denial causes.
  • Research denied claims and gather supporting documentation for reconsiderations and appeals.
  • Prepare, submit, and monitor appeals within payer-established deadlines.
  • Partner with billing, coding, clinical, utilization review, and authorization teams to resolve denial-related issues.
  • Maintain accurate denial logs, documentation, and follow-up records.
  • Post payments and adjustments accurately according to established procedures.
  • Monitor denial trends and identify recurring issues affecting reimbursement.
  • Escalate systemic payer, process, documentation, or authorization concerns to Revenue Cycle leadership.
  • Assist with payer audits, records requests, and supporting documentation submissions.
  • Develop and maintain denial tracking reports, dashboards, and performance metrics.
  • Support process improvement initiatives designed to reduce denials and improve cash collections.
  • Maintain compliance with payer contracts, regulatory requirements, organizational policies, and revenue cycle best practices.
  • Participate in departmental meetings, training, and continuous improvement activities.

Required Skills & Experience (Minimum Qualifications):

  • Associate degree in Healthcare Administration, Business, Accounting, Finance, or a related field; or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.
  • Two to four years of experience in healthcare billing, accounts receivable, denial management, revenue cycle operations, or a related healthcare finance function.
  • Strong understanding of insurance claim adjudication, reimbursement methodologies, and common denial causes, including medical necessity, authorization, coding, eligibility, and timely filing.
  • Working knowledge of payer requirements, appeal processes, deadlines, documentation standards, authorization requirements, and timely filing regulations.
  • Ability to read, interpret, and analyze Explanation of Benefits (EOBs), Electronic Remittance Advice (ERAs), remittance advice, and payer correspondence.
  • Working knowledge of ICD-10, CPT, and HCPCS coding concepts and their impact on claims processing, reimbursement, and denials.
  • Experience utilizing electronic health records (EHR), billing systems, and revenue cycle software platforms (such as Credible, Epic, Cerner, or similar systems).
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, denial tracking tools, spreadsheets, reporting dashboards, and data analysis tools used to monitor denial trends and reimbursement performance.
  • Strong analytical, organizational, problem-solving, and follow-through skills with a high degree of attention to detail.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, and maintain accuracy in a fast-paced environment.
  • At least 1 year of freedom from problematic substances.
  • Must be able to meet specific staff requirements outlined in Minnesota Statutes 245G.11.

  • Must successfully complete and maintain all required training and competency requirements applicable to the position prior to providing direct care or client services, including training related to client rights, confidentiality, mandated reporting, professional boundaries, and other applicable licensing and regulatory requirements.

jobs.title: Senior Strategic Growth Partner
jobs.excerpt: The RoleThis is a senior client-facing role for someone who wants to operate at the intersection of strategy, growth, sales, and execution.
jobs.description:
The Role

This is a senior client-facing role for someone who wants to operate at the intersection of strategy, growth, sales, and execution.

You will work directly with founders and business owners, understand their business in depth, identify what is holding growth back, and help them decide what to do next.

You are not here to simply manage a relationship.

You are here to become a trusted partner in the growth of the business.

That means understanding the client's goals, offer, market, acquisition strategy, sales process, delivery model, current constraints, and commercial priorities - then helping them turn that into a clear plan of action.

In some conversations, you will be helping a founder sharpen their positioning.

In others, you will be diagnosing why pipeline is weak, why sales are not converting, why execution is stalling, or where the next growth opportunity sits.

Your job is to create clarity. To tell clients what matters now. To show them what needs to happen next. And to make sure the right actions actually happen.

This is not a traditional Customer Success role.

It is a role for someone who wants to become an exceptional commercial operator by working closely with ambitious founders and helping them solve real business problems.

The Opportunity

You will have exposure to a large number of businesses, markets, offers, sales models, and growth challenges.

That creates an unusually steep learning curve.

Instead of spending years inside one company solving one set of problems, you will see patterns across dozens of businesses and develop the judgment to quickly understand:

  • What is actually holding growth back
  • What is noise and what matters
  • Where the highest-leverage opportunity is
  • What the founder should focus on now
  • What should be stopped
  • What should be doubled down on
  • How strategy should translate into execution

Over time, the expectation is that clients see you as someone whose judgment they trust.

Someone who can walk into a complicated situation, understand it quickly, simplify it, and give them a clear direction forward.

If you want to build serious capability in growth strategy, founder communication, sales, operations, and commercial decision-making, this role gives you the environment to do it.

What You Will Own

Become a True Growth Partner to Clients

You will work closely with founders to understand the business beyond surface-level account updates.

You will build a clear picture of:

  • Their business model
  • Target market
  • ICP
  • Offer
  • Pricing
  • Positioning
  • Acquisition channels
  • Sales process
  • Current pipeline
  • Delivery model
  • Team capacity
  • Growth goals
  • Immediate constraints

From there, you will help determine the highest-priority actions required to move the business forward.

Advise, Don't Just Support

We are not looking for someone who simply responds to questions.

We want someone capable of leading the thinking.

You should be comfortable saying:

"This is the problem I think we need to solve first."

"This is where I think you're focusing on the wrong thing."

"This is the strategy I would recommend."

"This is what I would do over the next 30 days."

"This is what needs to happen before we scale."

You will challenge clients when needed, simplify decisions, and help them avoid wasting time on low-leverage work.

Your value comes from your judgment, not just your responsiveness.

Turn Strategy Into Action

Good advice without execution is useless.

Every strategic conversation should translate into clear priorities.

You will help clients move from broad goals to focused execution:

  • Define the objective
  • Identify the constraint
  • Decide the strategy
  • Break it into clear actions
  • Assign ownership
  • Set timelines
  • Review what happened
  • Adjust based on results

You should naturally reduce complexity rather than add to it.

If a client has fifteen things they could be doing, your job is often to help them identify the two or three that actually matter.

Help Clients Build Revenue

You will think commercially.

That means understanding the complete journey from market to revenue:

Positioning → Acquisition → Conversations → Pipeline → Sales → Revenue → Delivery → Expansion

You will help clients understand where that journey is breaking down.

For example:

If acquisition is weak, you investigate the offer, market, message, and channel.

If leads are coming in but deals are not closing, you look at qualification, sales process, follow-up, positioning, and pricing.

If sales are happening but delivery is becoming difficult, you help identify what needs to change operationally.

You should be comfortable moving across the business rather than treating growth as a single function.

Work Across Growth Channels

Depending on the client, you may be advising across areas such as:

  • Cold email
  • Outbound
  • Paid acquisition
  • Offer development
  • ICP and positioning
  • Lead generation
  • CRM and pipeline
  • Sales process
  • Follow-up
  • Proposal strategy
  • Pricing
  • Go-to-market
  • Operational priorities
  • AI implementation and services

You do not need to personally be the world's best practitioner in every function.

You do need enough commercial understanding to identify what is working, what is not, ask the right questions, and make good strategic recommendations.

Lead High-Level Client Conversations

You will spend significant time speaking directly with founders and senior operators.

These are not scripted check-ins.

The conversations should be valuable enough that a founder would pay for the thinking itself.

You will:

  • Review business performance
  • Analyse what has changed
  • Identify opportunities
  • Diagnose problems
  • Challenge assumptions
  • Set priorities
  • Recommend strategy
  • Help unblock decisions
  • Create accountability
  • Keep momentum high

The standard is not whether the meeting happened.

The standard is whether the meeting changed what happens next.

Own the Bigger Picture

Clients may have multiple people supporting different parts of their business.

Your role is to maintain the full commercial picture.

You should understand what everyone is working on, how it connects to the overall strategy, and whether the combined effort is actually moving the client toward their objective.

If teams become disconnected, priorities conflict, or something important is falling through the cracks, you take ownership of resolving it.

The client should feel like they have one clear strategic partner who understands the whole business.

Identify Risk Before It Becomes a Problem

Strong operators notice problems early.

You should recognise when:

  • A client is losing momentum
  • Execution has stalled
  • The strategy is not producing results
  • Expectations have become misaligned
  • Lead flow is weak
  • Sales follow-up is poor
  • Internal delivery is becoming a blocker
  • The client is focusing on the wrong priorities
  • Trust is beginning to decline

Then act.

Do not wait for a formal escalation.

Part of being a trusted partner is being willing to address uncomfortable realities before they become larger problems.

Skills & Competencies

Commercial Judgment

You understand how businesses grow and make money.

You can connect strategy to revenue and distinguish between activity and actual commercial progress.

Strong Diagnostic Ability

You can listen to a complicated situation and quickly work out what the underlying issue is.

You separate symptoms from root causes.

Strategic Thinking

You can move between the big picture and immediate execution.

You know how to turn an ambitious goal into the next few actions that actually matter.

Founder-Level Communication

You can communicate confidently with intelligent, ambitious, demanding people.

You are comfortable challenging ideas without becoming confrontational.

You can give clear advice even when it is not what the client hoped to hear.

High Ownership

You do not wait to be told what to do when something is obviously not working.

You investigate, decide what needs to happen, and move it forward.

Structured Execution

You are excellent at turning conversations into decisions, priorities, actions, owners, and timelines.

Curiosity

You genuinely enjoy understanding businesses.

You want to know why an offer works.

Why one market responds differently from another.

Why one sales process converts and another does not.

Why certain founders execute faster than others.

That curiosity compounds into judgment.

AI Fluency

You actively use AI to improve your thinking and output.

You should use AI to analyse businesses, prepare for conversations, research markets, structure plans, review performance, document decisions, and increase the quality and speed of your work.

The Person We Want

This role is best suited to someone who wants to accelerate their career by taking on real responsibility.

You want to become the kind of person founders trust when making important decisions.

You want to develop judgment, not just knowledge.

You want to understand how businesses grow from the inside.

You are excited by the idea of working across many different companies, seeing patterns quickly, and becoming better at solving commercial problems every week.

You do not want to spend your career running scripted calls.

You want to sit across from a founder, understand what they are trying to build, and help them build it.

You Will Probably Not Fit If

  • You want a traditional Customer Success role
  • You prefer being given the answer rather than finding it
  • You are uncomfortable advising people more senior than you
  • You avoid giving direct recommendations
  • You prefer following scripts to thinking independently
  • You enjoy relationship management but are less interested in business strategy
  • You are uncomfortable discussing revenue, sales, pricing, or performance
  • You need very clear boundaries around your responsibilities
  • You focus heavily on activity rather than outcomes
  • You are looking for a low-pressure role with a predictable learning curve

Requirements

Experience

  • 7+ years in consulting, growth, client strategy, account management, sales, operations, or a senior client-facing role
  • Experience working directly with founders, executives, or business owners
  • Strong commercial understanding and the ability to think across acquisition, sales, and delivery
  • Experience helping businesses solve growth or execution problems
  • Strong understanding of B2B go-to-market
  • Direct exposure to areas such as outbound, sales, offer creation, paid acquisition, pipeline management, consulting, or agency delivery
  • Experience operating in fast-moving environments where judgment matters more than rigid process

Benefits

What You Get

  • Fully remote
  • Full-time role at a profitable, bootstrapped company
  • Direct access to ambitious founders and business owners
  • Exposure to a wide variety of companies, markets, and growth problems
  • The opportunity to build deep skill across strategy, acquisition, sales, operations, and AI
  • Significant autonomy and ownership
  • Direct access to senior leadership
  • A role where your judgment and capability can grow quickly
  • Performance-based progression into leadership, strategy, operations, or broader commercial ownership
  • Independent Contractor Agreement

This is an opportunity to become much more than an account manager.

Done well, this role develops you into the kind of commercial operator who can walk into almost any business, understand what matters, and help the founder decide what to do next.

Job Summary:

The Principal Compliance Specialist serves as the organization's subject matter authority for a defined regulatory domain or program area, independently managing complex and enterprise-scope matters from initiation through resolution without a defined playbook to follow. Operating across a large healthcare system, the Principal Specialist produces the analytical conclusions, regulatory interpretations, investigative findings, and policy recommendations that Directors and Executives rely on to make high-stakes compliance decisions. This role is the right fit for a seasoned compliance professional who wants to do the most intellectually demanding individual contributor work in the field, with direct visibility to senior leadership and enterprise-level impact, without moving into people management.

Job Duties:

  • Independently manages a defined compliance program area from annual work plan development through execution, monitoring, reporting, and closure without requiring supervisory structuring of tasks or priorities.
  • Analyzes complex and novel regulatory requirements, federal and state guidance documents, and enforcement trends; produces written regulatory impact analyses identifying the specific operational change required, the responsible business unit, and the recommended implementation timeline.
  • Designs and executes monitoring and auditing activities for assigned program areas, including selection of review methodology, sample design, data collection, findings documentation, and written presentation of results to the Manager or Director.
  • Leads compliance investigations assigned at the Principal level by coordinating information collection, conducting or managing interviews, documenting evidentiary findings, and producing a written investigative report that includes substantiation analysis and recommended corrective action for Director review.
  • Develops, drafts, and revises compliance policies, standards, and procedures for review and approval by the Director or Associate Officer; ensures each policy accurately reflects current regulatory requirements and is written to be operationally executable by the functions it governs.
  • Identifies compliance gaps through proactive program assessment; documents each gap with a risk severity rating using the function's established scoring methodology, a root cause analysis, and a recommended remediation plan with an assigned implementation owner.
  • Manages cross-functional compliance projects by developing the project work plan, assigning tasks to participating staff, tracking progress against established milestones, and escalating risks or delays to the Manager or Director with a documented options analysis.
  • Prepares written materials, including regulatory analysis memos, program status reports, and executive summary decks that communicate findings and recommendations to Director and VP-level leadership in a form suitable for executive review without additional editing.
  • Contributes to the annual enterprise compliance risk assessment by identifying and documenting risks within the assigned program area, scoring each risk using the function's established severity and likelihood methodology, and submitting a completed risk register section to the Director by the designated deadline.
  • Monitors published regulatory guidance, enforcement actions, and material industry developments relevant to the assigned domain on an ongoing basis; produces a written impact summary identifying the operational effect and recommended organizational response within 30 days of material issuance.
  • Serves as the primary compliance point of contact for assigned operational business partners; manages the relationship by conducting regular touchpoints, communicating program requirements, and tracking open compliance commitments to closure.

We are seeking a Senior Recruiter who thrives on the fast pace of full-cycle recruiting, someone who can juggle a full slate of open reqs without losing precision or creativity. You'll act as a trusted, consultative partner to hiring managers, running sourcing, screening, and candidate management day in and day out. You hold a rigorous bar for how candidates think, collaborate, and execute, and know how to balance that standard with the urgency of a scaling business, shaping how every candidate experiences our brand from first touchpoint to hire. You bring serious full-cycle recruiting chops, a sharp eye for data, and the kind of sourcing creativity that finds exceptional talent others overlook. Most importantly, you believe that who you hire defines the culture and capability of everything a company builds. If you're energized by the challenge of attracting top-tier talent to a product that's transforming an industry, this role was made for you.

Why Tenna?

At Tenna, we believe the best is right in front of all of us, and that each day holds more potential than the one before. We believe that every new discovery can lead to something better than we thought possible. When we boil it down, the top five qualities that define the Tenna Team are quality-obsessed, gritty, continuous learners, collaborative problem solvers, and just plain awesome. Sound like you? Join us as we empower our customers to control their mixed assets anytime, anywhere, on one comprehensive platform. Apply now!

Responsibilities

  • Own full-cycle recruiting for a portfolio of open requisitions, partnering closely with hiring managers to understand role needs and deliver a consistent, high-quality candidate pipeline.
  • Collaborate with leadership and Hiring Managers to anticipate talent needs and establish proactive sourcing pipelines.
  • Analyze external labor market data and internal talent gaps to develop sourcing strategies by function and level.
  • Conduct quarterly reviews of hiring needs and adjust the strategy to support seasonal or shifting demand.
  • Partners with the Director of Human Resources to identify opportunities for internal mobility and succession-based hiring pipelines.
  • Own and optimize the candidate journey from sourcing to onboarding, ensuring every touchpoint reflects Tenna’s core values positively.
  • Maintain a clean, organized, and up-to-date ATS, including but not limited to candidate notes, disqualification reasons, job statuses, and tagging, to ensure accurate reporting and compliance.
  • Ensure that all recruiting data is clean and auditable. Conduct periodic ATS audits and train stakeholders on best practices for data hygiene as needed.
  • Maintain SLAs with hiring managers, facilitate kickoff and debrief sessions, and provide training to ensure best-in-class (consistent and objective) hiring practices.
  • Identify, coordinate, and execute recruiting event attendance, including career fairs, virtual hiring days, university meetups, hackathons, and community initiatives.
  • Build relationships with external organizations, boot camps, etc. to expand event reach and increase candidate flow.
  • Build and maintain a database of high-potential passive candidates through research, networking, and direct sourcing efforts.
  • Utilize Boolean search techniques to identify and engage passive candidates through advanced search logic.
  • Leverage social media platforms (e.g., LinkedIn, X/Twitter, GitHub, Slack communities) to source talent and promote open roles.
  • Engage with niche and industry-specific job boards to attract candidates with specialized skill sets.
  • Promote our referral programs to drive warm leads and expand candidate reach through internal networks.
  • Proactively create and adapt candidate outreach strategies on sourcing platforms to improve engagement and pipeline performance.
  • Ensure all recruiting activities comply with relevant employment laws, including EEO, OFCCP, and GDPR/CCPA, as applicable.

Requirements

  • 7+ years of progressive experience in full-cycle talent acquisition.
  • Experience supporting a high-growth and/or fast-paced company is strongly preferred.
  • Proven success hiring across technical, corporate, and high-volume roles.
  • Proven success in strategic sourcing, candidate evaluation, and stakeholder partnership across multiple functions and levels.
  • Hands-on experience using ATS platforms such as Greenhouse, Lever, Workday, or iCIMS to manage workflows, data, and compliance.
  • Demonstrated ability to analyze recruiting funnel data and use insights to recommend and implement process improvements.
  • Strong experience with Microsoft Suite: Excel, Word, PPT, and Outlook.
  • Demonstrated ability to build and sustain effective relationships with internal stakeholders, hiring managers, and external partners.
  • Diligent, thorough, and detail-oriented.
  • Proven ability to manage confidential and sensitive information.
  • Deadline-driven with a strong sense of urgency and accountability to meet business hiring goals.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence and consult across all levels of the organization.
  • Experienced in handling confidential and sensitive information with discretion and integrity.
  • Self-starter with a service-oriented mindset, capable of adapting to shifting priorities and taking ownership of outcomes.
  • Bachelor’s Degree in a business-related major is required or equivalent.

jobs.description:
Expression of Interest · Inquire First

We are meeting senior leaders for this planned function as we fundraise. This is an exploratory conversation, not an immediately funded salaried vacancy or a guaranteed start date. No cash salary is available today; any equity arrangement must be agreed separately. You are not being asked to begin work by expressing interest.

Use the Apply form below to introduce yourself and indicate your interest. We can discuss mutual fit, scope, funding, compensation, and timing before either side makes a commitment.

Remote · United States · Full time · Functional leadership

Determine when a market simulation deserves to influence a business decision. Build the evaluation function that makes model quality, failure modes, and release tradeoffs visible to research, product, and customers.

Why Subconscious

Subconscious is building the intelligence to run the economy. We start with a simulator for business decisions, using causal experiments on simulated markets to test products, pricing, messaging, and go-to-market choices before capital is committed. The long-term ambition is to help businesses discover unmet demand and build around what people actually need.

The function you will build

Own evaluation strategy, benchmark governance, regression criteria, and the model-quality hiring plan. Define the evidence required for release decisions and escalate unsupported claims. Partner with causal research on validity and with engineering on reliable execution of evaluations.

This is a hands-on leadership role. Set the functional roadmap and propose staffing and spending priorities with the founding team. Hiring and budget commitments depend on approved resources; an established team or funded budget is not assumed.

Proposed first 90 days after joining

Use these as an initial agenda, refined with the founders against the product, customer needs, and resources at your start.

  • Inventory model claims and customer use cases; map each to a testable question and an appropriate reference or human baseline.

  • Build reproducible evaluation sets with clear provenance, held-out testing, leakage controls, and uncertainty estimates.

  • Establish failure analysis across populations, decision types, and distribution shifts, including cases where fluent output gives a misleading impression of quality.

  • Create a release review that records tradeoffs among quality, latency, cost, and known limitations.

How we will judge progress

Evaluation results are reproducible, regressions are detected before release, and aggregate scores do not conceal important failures. Track coverage of consequential use cases, benchmark stability, error by relevant cohort, and time from diagnosis to a verified improvement.

What you bring

  • You have led evaluation, measurement, or model-quality programs and can show decisions that changed because of the evidence.

  • You are strong in statistics and practical ML evaluation, with hands-on ability to build data and analysis pipelines.

  • You can challenge a promising result constructively, investigate confounding or leakage, and explain why a metric is or is not useful.

We are looking for evidence of judgment, execution, and leadership. A particular company pedigree or previous executive title is not a substitute for that evidence.

Compensation and funding

We are actively fundraising. Only equity-based compensation is currently available; no cash salary is available today. The equity grant and its terms have not been set for this role and must be agreed before joining. Any future salary, incentive plan, benefits, hiring budget, or paid start date depends on financing and written agreement. Funding and its timing are not guaranteed.

Before deciding to join, discuss the grant structure, fully diluted ownership basis, vesting, dilution, applicable exercise terms, company funding position, and working arrangement. A company valuation is not the cash value of an equity grant.

How we work

Remote · United States. The planned role is full time; timing is to be agreed. Expect direct collaboration with the founders, work across scientific and commercial boundaries, and responsibility for doing the early work yourself. The current role does not include visa sponsorship. Confirm practical collaboration hours and any travel expectations during the initial conversation.

Start with work you already own

Describe an evaluation that contradicted an attractive headline result. How did you establish the failure, and what changed in the model, product, or release decision?

Please do not share confidential employer or customer materials. Bring your questions about our product, evidence, team, finances, and the authority attached to the role. Mutual diligence matters for a decision of this size.

jobs.excerpt: Ready to own it, build it, and grow it? The MissionPublitas turns static, dead PDFs into interactive, shoppable digital content discovery experiences.
jobs.description:
Ready to own it, build it, and grow it?

The Mission

Publitas turns static, dead PDFs into interactive, shoppable digital content discovery experiences. For our global enterprise clients, transforming their traditional assets requires seamless technical alignment, strategic onboarding, and flawless execution.

Your mission as Project Manager is to take end-to-end ownership of complex enterprise SaaS implementation projects, guiding major brands from initial onboarding to successful expansion. We work 80% asynchronously and judge success entirely by your ability to manage risks, align stakeholders, and deliver measurable customer value, not by the number of hours you sit on Zoom.

What Success Looks Like (Your First 90 Days)

We don't measure you only by years of experience; we look at how effectively you take ownership, learn our environment, and deliver results. Here is what we expect you to achieve in your first 3 months:

Day 30: You have built a strong understanding of the Publitas product suite, value proposition, and delivery methodologies. You have shadowed active implementation projects and started taking ownership of your first client projects and stakeholder communication.

Day 60: You are independently managing client implementations, including scoping discussions, timeline planning, stakeholder communication, and cross-functional coordination. You can identify risks early, make practical decisions, and escalate when needed rather than relying on close day-to-day guidance.

Day 90: You have successfully delivered your first enterprise implementation project from kickoff to launch. You have established trusted relationships with client and internal stakeholders and are confidently managing your own project portfolio with a high degree of autonomy.

Requirements

The DNA of a Project Manager at Publitas (Culture & Ownership)

High Ownership Delivery: You don't just pass messages between clients and developers; you take responsibility for moving projects forward from start to finish. You proactively identify risks, keep stakeholders aligned, manage priorities, and drive projects to completion. You are comfortable making decisions independently while knowing when something needs additional input or escalation.

Collaborative Bridge-Builder: You thrive at the intersection of client management and technical execution. You can confidently manage conversations with German-speaking enterprise clients and work closely with our technical teams to scope API integrations, custom development workflows, analytics setups, and other implementation requirements. You don't need to be an engineer, but you are comfortable working with technical topics and asking the right questions.

High Autonomy, Zero Ego: In a remote-first, asynchronous environment, you are highly organized, proactive, and comfortable managing your own workload. You don't need constant direction to know what should happen next. You take initiative, communicate clearly, and focus on outcomes while actively collaborating and asking for input when it improves the result.

Continuous Improvement Mindset: You already have a strong foundation in project management and are looking to deepen your experience with enterprise SaaS delivery. You learn from each project, share what works, and contribute ideas that make our delivery processes clearer, faster, and more effective.

What We Offer You to Win

  • Competitive Compensation: A competitive salary geo-bracketed to your location.

  • True Remote Autonomy: No clock-watching or useless alignment meetings. You manage your projects and schedule independently.

  • Global Team Retreats: Working remotely shouldn't mean working isolated. We gather the entire company in inspiring cities across the globe once a year to connect, strategize, and celebrate in person.

  • Modern Stack & Gear: A top-tier MacBook, remote work accessories, and a co-working allowance if you prefer to work outside your home.

  • Personal Growth Budget: A monthly wellness allowance, an education/course budget to sharpen your skills, and free access to Kindle and Audible books.

  • Time Off & Perks: 25 days of paid vacation plus your local national holidays, along with free Publitas Swag.

The Non-Negotiables

  • Fluent German & English: You will navigate complex enterprise client conversations in German and collaborate with our global, distributed team in English.

  • 3+ Years SaaS Implementation Experience: You have a proven track record of managing and delivering complex, technical enterprise SaaS project lifecycles from onboarding to expansion, ideally within retail, publishing, or marketing tech.

  • Technical & Commercial Acumen: You are deeply familiar with project management tools (Agile, Asana, Jira) and possess a solid understanding of HTML, design tools, analytics, APIs, and custom integrations to effectively scope technical client requirements.

  • AI-First Execution: We do not scale headcount to solve manual problems. You must have a proven track record of working in an AI-first way, leveraging generative AI tools to hyper-personalize communications, automate project documentation, summarize meeting data, and accelerate your delivery velocity.

At Publitas, we see AI as a core lever for performance, efficiency, and innovation. We expect all team members to actively use AI in their daily work to improve quality, speed, and output.

Depending on the role, this ranges from effectively using AI tools in day-to-day workflows to designing and scaling AI-driven systems. We are not looking for candidates who are “AI-curious”; we look for people who already use AI to do better work and can demonstrate tangible impact.

jobs.title: VP of Marketing
jobs.excerpt: FOR THE RIGHT PERSON, THIS IS THE OPPORTUNITY OF A CAREERBefore you read another word, ask yourself one question: Are you the kind of person who wants to build something with a company that has been in business for 25 years, has a stellar reputation, is ranked in the top 10 in the world at what they do, yet no one knows who they are?
jobs.description:
FOR THE RIGHT PERSON, THIS IS THE OPPORTUNITY OF A CAREER

Before you read another word, ask yourself one question: Are you the kind of person who wants to build something with a company that has been in business for 25 years, has a stellar reputation, is ranked in the top 10 in the world at what they do, yet no one knows who they are? I am not sure you even knew who PlanITROI was before reading this.

Gartner, Microsoft, the International Association of IT Asset Managers, and many more recognize PlanITROI as the world's leader in Lifecycle Services and IT Asset Disposition, focused on reuse as intended use.

We are the world's leader in transforming someone's nothing and turning it into someone's everything. We have created our own 501(c)(3) called the Digital Dreams Project, where we have impacted over 1 million people's lives who needed affordable technology. This story has never been told properly. We are looking for the right person who can tell the story. For the right person, this is the most important opportunity they will read this year.

If this sounds like the kind of challenge and opportunity you have been looking for, keep reading.

Celebrating 25 years in business, PlanITROI is the world's greatest Lifecycle Services and ITAD company.

PlanITROI is committed to the future of lifecycle services, often coined and built terminology used around the globe. The phrase "reuse as intended use," now used by analysts at Gartner, was coined by PlanITROI. We are also the world's leader in delivering repaired, refurbished, and re-certified computing technology directly to the next user, and we are the top key supplier to organizations like Best Buy, Walmart, Target, eBay, Amazon, etc. We are an asset to businesses that need this in their portfolio. Corporations like GSK, Procter & Gamble, Visa, and Paycom count on our lifecycle services to provide data destruction and other critical services that keep their technology lifecycles running.

PlanITROI is ready to invest in the brand, inbound engine, website, thought leadership platform, and PR presence we have earned and deserve. You will build all of it. Everything you create will be yours. You are coming into a world-class, 25-year-old organization with a story that has never been told the way it deserves to be told. You are the architect.

You own it, you solve it, and you get it done.

The mission matters too. This is not another B2B software company selling platforms. PlanITROI exists to provide affordable technology to people who need it most. Over 1 million lives have been changed through our Digital Dreams program. That combination of enterprise credibility, 25 years of operational excellence, and genuine social purpose is almost impossible to find in a senior B2B marketing role. It exists here.

You will market to the most prestigious ICP worldwide. Fortune 500 companies, global financial institutions, major healthcare systems, and federal agencies. Every piece of content you create, every campaign you launch, every story you tell is aimed at the people who run technology at the largest organizations on earth. That is a career-defining stage. You will have a direct line to a visionary leadership team that thinks in decades, not quarters, and that will trust you to translate that vision into a brand the market cannot ignore.

You will have a level of access, trust, and ownership that creates a rare opportunity to make a lasting impact.

When you deliver, the path to CMO is real, and it is fast. PlanITROI is scaling and at its next stage of growth. The person who builds this marketing function owns everything that comes after it.

ARE YOU THE RIGHT FIT? ASK YOURSELF THESE QUESTIONS

The right person for this role will read this list and feel energized. If you can answer yes to everything here, we want to hear from you.

  • You are energized by the opportunity to build from the ground up at a company with 25 years of reputation and credibility. A blank canvas and real ownership excite you.
  • You have a trusted network of freelancers, content creators, video producers, and specialist resources you can deploy.
  • You have personally owned a full website rebuild from strategy through launch, and you can point us to the live site.
  • You think strategically and know how to direct specialists. You bring the vision and the plan.
  • You can form a clear, confident point of view quickly. You listen deeply, learn the business, and turn what you learn into a concrete plan.
  • You research before you contact us. You understand PlanITROI, our competitors, and where there is opportunity for growth.
  • Digital Dreams and the impact on more than 1 million lives genuinely move you. The mission is part of the reason you want to show up.

WHAT WE ARE TRYING TO SOLVE

PlanITROI has built a world-class operation, but our brand, digital presence, and marketing engine have not kept pace with the company we have become. We are too invisible in the channels where our future clients are researching, learning, and making decisions. We lack a cohesive marketing strategy and the infrastructure to execute one consistently. Our story, our capabilities, our innovation, and our impact are not reaching the people who need to hear them.

This role exists to close that gap through strategic leadership, modern marketing expertise, and the brand infrastructure required to make PlanITROI impossible to ignore.

WHAT YOU MUST BRING WITH YOU ON DAY ONE

PlanITROI is ready to invest and build at the speed envisioned; you must arrive already equipped.

We are not constructing a large internal marketing department on day one. The expectation is that you bring a trusted bench of external resources who know how you operate and can begin contributing immediately.

If you can answer yes to all six questions below, you are exactly the kind of marketing leader we want to meet.

  1. Do you have freelancers, content creators, video producers, designers, and other specialists you could activate in your first week?
  2. Do you have PR and media contacts in B2B technology or IT services who know you and will take your call?
  3. Do you have web development and design partners you trust to execute a full website rebuild?
  4. Do you have SEO, GEO, and AEO capability either within your own practice or through a proven partner?
  5. Have you successfully directed specialist agencies toward clearly scoped deliverables without becoming dependent on large retainers or losing control of the strategy?
  6. Do you have a fully formed, opinionated point of view on what a modern B2B inbound engine looks like and a track record of building one?

WHAT THE PERFECT CANDIDATE LOOKS LIKE

  • You have built your career in growth-stage or mid-market B2B technology environments where resources were lean, the playbook was not handed to you, and the results were yours to own.
  • You are comfortable operating in a fast-paced environment where momentum, responsiveness, and high-quality execution matter.
  • You have marketed to Fortune 500 procurement leaders, global CIOs, IT Directors, and enterprise decision-makers. You understand their buying cycles, their language, and what gets their attention.
  • Your background includes B2B hardware, IT services, managed services, device lifecycle, SaaS, or an adjacent technology category.
  • You are equally comfortable developing the story and building the machine that delivers it.
  • You understand the difference between pursuing perfection and delivering excellent work with speed, judgment, and attention to detail.

This role operates in Eastern Time.

Qualifications & Requirements:

  • 10+ years of progressive B2B marketing experience with significant leadership responsibility.
  • Growth-stage or startup background where you personally built marketing infrastructure, teams, programs, and processes.
  • Enterprise B2B ICP fluency, including experience marketing to Fortune 500 and global enterprise buyers.
  • B2B technology background, ideally in hardware, IT services, managed services, lifecycle services, SaaS, or an adjacent category.
  • Proven brand builder with experience developing positioning, messaging, and market presence.
  • Storyteller and executor: Writes compelling narratives AND builds the systems that deliver them at scale.
  • Demonstrated PR and thought leadership results.
  • Experience owning a full website rebuild from strategy through launch.
  • Strong command of modern marketing tools, AI, automation, and data.
  • Practical understanding of SEO, GEO, and AEO.
  • Ready-to-deploy network of external marketing specialists and resources.
  • Strong vendor manager: Builds lean teams, deploys external resources strategically, and holds every person and agency accountable to specific outcomes and deadlines.
  • Agile under pressure and comfortable adapting as priorities evolve.
  • Thinks in years and executes in weeks.
  • Owns the role: Sets priorities, meets deadlines, holds themselves to high standards, and communicates proactively.
  • Mission-driven: PlanITROI's Digital Dreams program has impacted over 1 million lives with affordable technology. If that does not genuinely move you, this is not the right role.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Website Strategy & Rebuild

  • Lead the end-to-end strategic rebuilding of the PlanITROI website.
  • Audit existing sites across SEO, GEO, AEO, conversion, content, messaging, and user experience.
  • Create a digital experience that tells the full PlanITROI story and positions the company as the market leader.
  • Own the project roadmap and timeline; manage every internal and external resource through execution and launch with clear accountability to agreed timelines and outcomes.

Thought Leadership & PR

  • Build and execute a thought leadership strategy that establishes PlanITROI and its executives as recognized voices in Lifecycle Services, ITAD, sustainability, reuse, and the circular economy.
  • Develop executive narratives, byline content, speaking opportunities, media relationships, and industry visibility.
  • Build a proactive PR engine that earns meaningful coverage and strengthens market reputation.

Inbound Marketing & Digital Visibility

  • Build a modern B2B inbound marketing engine from the ground up.
  • Develop strategies that increase visibility, engagement, qualified traffic, and enterprise opportunities.
  • Own SEO, GEO, AEO, content strategy, campaign strategy, digital performance, and attribution.
  • Ensure PlanITROI is visible wherever enterprise buyers are researching Lifecycle Services and ITAD solutions.

Brand Strategy & Messaging

  • Clarify and strengthen brand positioning, messaging, and brand architecture.
  • Translate a complex 25-year company story into clear, compelling language the market understands.
  • Create consistency across digital, sales, executive communications, events, PR, and customer-facing materials.
  • Build a brand that reflects the quality, innovation, scale, and impact of the organization behind it.

Executive Presence & Physical Events

  • Build the strategy that strengthens PlanITROI's executive presence in the market.
  • Identify and pursue high-value speaking opportunities, conferences, industry events, and thought leadership platforms.
  • Ensure physical events reinforce the broader brand and growth strategy rather than operating as isolated marketing activities.

Team Building & External Resource Management

  • Build a lean, high-output marketing function.
  • Determine what capabilities belong internally and what should be supported through specialized external resources.
  • Hold every external vendor and resource accountable to clear deadlines, defined quality standards, and measurable outcomes, with a strong focus on results.
  • Provide clear strategic direction so specialists understand exactly what they are building, why it matters, and what success looks like.
  • Identify capacity or capability gaps early and bring forward practical, costed solutions.

30 / 60 / 90-DAY PLAN

  • First 30 Days: Listen, Learn, and Assess
  • Days 31 to 60: Build the Foundation
  • Days 61 to 90: Launch and Measure

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE AT ONE YEAR

By year one, PlanITROI looks and sounds like the market industry leader it is. Our website is a powerful sales and recruiting asset, our brand is consistent and recognizable, and our thought leadership is reaching the right audiences. Inbound opportunities are growing with clear attribution, sales have a strong content engine supporting active deals, and our executives are earning greater visibility through publishing, media, and speaking opportunities. The marketing function operates with clear strategy, ownership, and measurable results.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE AT THREE YEARS

By year three, PlanITROI is a recognized category leader in Lifecycle Services and ITAD. We are on the shortlist for major enterprise opportunities because the market already knows and trusts our brand. Inbound marketing is a meaningful contributor to revenue, Digital Dreams is recognized as a powerful ESG differentiator, and our brand, reputation, and thought leadership create a competitive advantage that is difficult to replicate. The leader who built it has earned the opportunity to step into the CMO role.

WHO WINS AT PlanITROI

The marketing leaders who thrive at PlanITROI share a few important qualities. They can translate our story in a way that resonates with the market, balance strategic thinking with strong execution, and remain curious and open to new approaches. jobs.description:
Position Summary

The Director I of Catastrophe Modeling leads catastrophe risk analytics for the Central Underwriting organization, sitting at the intersection of modeling science, data engineering, and underwriting strategy. This role owns both the technical execution of cat modeling (RMS, AIR) and the tooling, pipelines, and automation that make that modeling fast, accurate, and scalable — while building and managing the team that delivers it. The Director translates portfolio-level model output into underwriting guidance, sets technical standards for the function, and represents catastrophe risk analytics to underwriting and executive leadership.

What will your job entail?

What You’ll Do

Team & Strategic Leadership

  • Build, manage, and mentor a team blending catastrophe modeling analysts and technical/automation developers.
  • Mentor, guide, and train portfolio modeling managers across the team, building bench strength and consistent technical standards for the broader cat modeling function.
  • Set the technical roadmap and priorities for cat modeling, data engineering, and reporting tooling in support of Central Underwriting.
  • Serve as the primary bridge between catastrophe modeling analytics and underwriting leadership, translating model output into underwriting guidance and appetite decisions.
  • Represent catastrophe risk analytics in executive and reinsurance discussions, including cat event response briefings.

Portfolio Rollups & External Delivery

  • Coordinate Analyze Re-related portfolio rollups, ensuring consistent, accurate aggregation across books of business.
  • Oversee delivery of portfolio and modeling outputs to external carriers and reinsurance partners, ensuring accuracy, timeliness, and consistency of format.
  • Partner with reinsurance and ceded-re contacts to align rollup structures and delivery cadence with treaty and program needs.

Research & Advanced Analytics

  • Lead research initiatives that extend advanced analytics capabilities within the catastrophe modeling domain (e.g., secondary uncertainty, model blending, climate-adjusted view of risk).
  • Evaluate emerging modeling science, vendor model updates, and academic/industry research for applicability to the portfolio.
  • Champion a culture of continuous improvement, piloting new methods and tools ahead of enterprise-wide adoption.

Cross-Functional Partnership

  • Partner closely with Capital Management, Pricing, Reserving, and Data Engineering to streamline processes and align catastrophe outputs with capital, pricing, and reserving needs.
  • Standardize handoffs and data contracts between cat modeling and these partner teams to reduce rework and improve turnaround.

Vendor & Tooling Engagement

  • Own vendor and platform strategy for RMS and AIR, including licensing, upgrades, and platform roadmap decisions.
  • Lead evaluation and assessment of tools and vendors for specific perils, models, and IT infrastructure, including Analyze Re and emerging modeling platforms.
  • Build the business case for new tooling or vendor changes, balancing analytical capability, cost, and infrastructure fit.

Modeling & Portfolio Analytics

  • Oversee catastrophe modeling using RMS and AIR across multiple lines of business, ensuring quality and consistency of account, portfolio, and reinsurance-layer analyses.
  • Direct the production of portfolio-level metrics — PML, AAL, exposed limits, EP curves (OEP/AEP), and tail-risk/TVaR measures — used in underwriting and reinsurance decisions.
  • Set standards for exposure data preparation, validation, and cleansing prior to model runs.
  • Lead catastrophe event response for the underwriting organization, ensuring rapid, accurate exposure summaries and loss estimates.

Data Engineering, Tooling & Automation

  • Direct the design of ETL pipelines and data pipelines that ingest and normalize exposure data (policy schedules, CRE, shapefiles) to RMS/AIR data standards.
  • Oversee development of automated AIR/RMS workflow utilities (imports/exports, batch runs, result extraction, QA checks) and reusable reporting assets in SQL, Python, R, and Excel/VBA.
  • Champion adoption of Azure Databricks and cloud-based analytics (PySpark, Delta Lake) as the future-state platform for modeling data and results.
  • Ensure data quality controls, QA dashboards, and documentation/SOPs are in place and consistently followed across the team.

Tech Stack

  • Modeling Platforms: RMS (Risk Modeler, Underwrite IQ), AIR (Touchstone), and Analyze Re for portfolio rollups.
  • Languages & Tools: SQL, Python, R, VBA, Alteryx (Designer and Server).
  • Data: Exposure schedules, shapefiles, ELTs/EDMs, event results, treaty structures.
  • Cloud: Azure Databricks, Azure Data Lake/Blob, Delta Lake (strongly preferred).

Qualifications

Required

  • 8+ years of progressive experience in catastrophe modeling, portfolio risk analytics, or cat-modeling-adjacent data engineering, including prior people leadership or team-lead experience managing other modeling professionals or managers.
  • Deep hands-on proficiency in RMS and/or AIR Touchstone — exposure preparation, batch processing, results extraction, and interpretation of EP curves and loss tables.
  • Strong SQL skills and demonstrated experience directing or building automation with Python, R, VBA, and/or Alteryx.
  • Track record of translating catastrophe model output into underwriting or portfolio management decisions.
  • Proven ability to lead teams through real-time catastrophe event response.
  • Experience coordinating portfolio rollups and external deliverables to carriers or reinsurance partners.
  • Demonstrated experience partnering cross-functionally with groups such as Capital Management, Pricing, Reserving, or Data Engineering.
  • Excellent communication skills, with experience presenting technical analysis to underwriting and executive stakeholders.

Preferred / Nice-to-Have

  • Experience with Analyze Re or comparable portfolio roll-up/aggregation platforms.
  • Experience with Azure Databricks, PySpark, and Delta Lake / data lakehouse patterns.
  • Knowledge of reinsurance structures and portfolio risk metrics (PML, AAL, TVaR).
  • Familiarity with geospatial data handling and mapping (geopandas, shapefiles, spatial joins).
  • Experience with version control (Git) and SDLC practices (branching, code review, release management).
  • Prior experience leading vendor evaluations for modeling platforms, peril models, or analytics infrastructure.
  • Background in or exposure to applied research within catastrophe modeling or a related quantitative discipline.

Core Competencies

  • Leadership: Builds and develops technical teams and mentors other managers; sets clear priorities and holds a high bar for quality.
  • Strategic & Analytical Thinking: Connects portfolio model output to underwriting strategy and enterprise risk appetite.
  • Technical Depth: Retains credibility with hands-on modelers and developers while operating at a leadership level.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Builds durable partnerships with Capital Management, Pricing, Reserving, and Data Engineering.
  • Communication: Clearly conveys technical insight to underwriting, executive, and reinsurance audiences.
  • Execution & Automation Mindset: Prioritizes scalable, repeatable tooling over one-off analysis.
  • Curiosity & Research Orientation: Continually pushes the domain forward through new methods and advanced analytics.

jobs.description:
About AI Acquisition

AI Acquisition is a bootstrapped, multi-entity business helping founders and operators scale with AI. We combine SaaS platforms, consulting, and a full sales and delivery engine. We manage thousands of active clients across multiple products and operate globally.

The Role

You're taking over an existing book of established client relationships. These are not new clients figuring out what they bought. They've been with us, they know the product, and they have expectations built on months of experience with the business.

Your job is to keep them progressing, keep them retained, and keep them expanding. That means understanding where each client actually is in their business, what's working, what's stuck, and what they need next. Not checking in for the sake of it. Actually moving the needle on their results.

This is a consulting role disguised as account management. You're not managing a spreadsheet of renewals. You're advising business owners on how to grow: how to frame their offer, how to think about their funnel, how to close deals, how to handle fulfillment, and how to use AI to do all of it faster.

The clients you inherit will have history, context, and in some cases, frustrations that predate you. Your first job is to audit that book, understand every account's real status, and earn trust through competence rather than promises.

Requirements

What You'll Own

  • An established portfolio of legacy clients across various stages of maturity and engagement
  • Regular check-ins, growth workshops, and strategic conversations with business owners who are building and scaling real companies
  • Client retention — spotting risk before it becomes a refund conversation, re-engaging clients who've gone quiet, and resolving issues without escalation
  • Business consulting — advising clients on offer framing, lead generation strategy, sales process, prospecting, closing, and fulfillment. You need to understand these well enough to coach, not just relay information
  • Upsell identification — knowing when a client is ready for more and positioning the next step as the natural move, not a sales pitch
  • Cross-functional coordination with the onboarding, deliverables, and office hours teams to make sure nothing falls through the cracks
  • Documentation — every interaction, decision, and next step logged so anyone picking up your account knows exactly where things stand

What We Need From You

  • Native or near-native English fluency is non-negotiable. You will be on camera with clients daily and every conversation needs to land with clarity and confidence
  • Direct experience as a CSM, account manager, or business consultant where you personally advised clients on how to start, grow, or scale a business. Not just managed the relationship, actually consulted on the business itself
  • You understand the mechanics of lead generation, sales funnels, cold email, LinkedIn outreach, and how they connect to a client's revenue. You don't need to execute campaigns yourself but you need to diagnose why one isn't converting and coach the client through it
  • You've managed a portfolio of clients where retention and expansion were your responsibility, not someone else's
  • You're comfortable with difficult conversations. Clients who are frustrated, clients who are stuck, clients who need honest feedback about their own execution. You handle these with composure and directness
  • You come with solutions, not just problems. When something breaks in a client's journey, your instinct is to propose the fix, not report the issue and wait
  • You pick things up fast. The biggest challenge for external hires in this role has been the knowledge gap — there is a lot to learn about our products, processes, and client journeys, and you need to absorb it quickly enough to be credible in front of clients within weeks, not months
  • You're comfortable with AI tools and either already use them in your work or will learn without being told to

This Is Not For You If

  • You only know relationship management without the business consulting layer. "Keeping clients happy" is not the job. Moving their business forward is
  • You need months to ramp before you can have a real conversation with a client. Our clients won't wait that long
  • You're uncomfortable advising business owners on sales, prospecting, or offer strategy. That's a core part of the role, not a nice-to-have
  • You avoid hard conversations or tell clients what they want to hear instead of what they need to hear
  • You wait to be told what's wrong rather than finding it yourself

What Success Looks Like

  • Your clients are progressing, not just retained. Business results, not just satisfaction scores
  • Clients at risk are flagged and handled before they escalate. You're the person who prevents the refund conversation, not the one having it
  • You've audited your book within the first two weeks and can articulate every client's real status, not what's in the notes
  • You're coaching clients on their business, not just updating them on deliverables
  • You pick up the product knowledge fast enough to be credible in front of clients by week three
  • You adopt new tools and processes without being chased

Benefits

The Environment

This is a high-performance, remote-first team at the cutting edge of AI-powered business building.

  • Direct access to department heads from day one
  • Strong performers progress quickly based on what they deliver, not tenure
  • Exposure to AI-led systems and tools daily
  • Autonomy and ownership over your portfolio
  • A team that holds a high bar and expects the same from everyone

This role operates as an independent contractor engagement: invoice-based, permanent structure, regulated notice periods on both sides. We expect 50 to 60 hours a week from our best people, not as a crunch but as the natural shape of work that matters.

If you're looking for structure handed to you, this isn't the right place. If you want to be the one "Lifting the Hood", build something real, and raise the bar every week with a team that moves fast, we want to talk.
