Job Details

Reporting to the National Vice President, Commercial Strategy and Business Optimization (CRLTC), the Director, Commercial Strategy & GPO Management advances CRLTC’s commercial strategy and governance of GPO and Buying Group relationships. The role focuses on portfolio discipline, deal committee leadership, analytical decision support, partnership governance, and execution across priority commercial opportunities.

This leader partners with the NVP to translate portfolio priorities, GPO objectives, and Buying Group strategy into clear governance routines, stakeholder alignment, and decision-ready recommendations. The role supports customer, segment, GPO, and Buying Group-specific commercial approaches and ensures key opportunities, renewals, partnership commitments, and market-share objectives are evaluated against enterprise strategy, pricing guardrails, profitability goals, and value objectives.

The Director partners across Sales, Pricing, Commercial Finance, SmartSource, Strategic Global Sourcing, Supply Chain/USSC, Commercial Excellence, Legal/Contracting, segment leadership, and Buying Group stakeholders to improve visibility, rigor, and alignment across CRLTC commercial priorities.

Primary Duties and Responsibilities:

1) Commercial strategy governance and portfolio coordination

  • Support and operationalize CRLTC’s commercial strategy by establishing and maintaining governance routines that improve visibility, prioritization, and alignment across the commercial portfolio.

  • Maintain a structured view of key renewals, strategic prospects, Buying Group and GPO-related priorities, and other high-impact opportunities requiring elevated commercial engagement.

  • Partner with segment leadership and cross-functional stakeholders to ensure opportunity priorities, risks, decisions, and next steps are visible and aligned to CRLTC portfolio objectives.

  • Help translate enterprise and segment priorities into repeatable governance processes, standardized materials, and clear accountability across internal teams.

2) Commercial deal governance, strategy, and value realization

  • Lead CRLTC commercial strategy and deal committee forums, ensuring priority opportunities are brought forward with clear context, stakeholder input, decision needs, and recommended path forward.

  • Maintain disciplined intake, prioritization, and review processes for renewals, acquisitions, strategic customer opportunities, Buying Group strategy decisions, and GPO-related decisions.

  • Develop decision-ready materials that clarify customer context, strategic objectives, pricing considerations, economics, risks, trade-offs, approval needs, and recommended actions.

  • Use data-driven analysis and financial insight to assess customer economics, Buying Group performance, profitability drivers, pricing scenarios, contract terms, share-of-wallet opportunities, leakage, and enterprise trade-offs.

  • Partner with Sales, Pricing, Finance, Buying Group leadership, and other stakeholders to shape customer-specific and group-level strategies within enterprise pricing guardrails and value objectives.

  • Coordinate movement from strategy through governance, approval, contracting, implementation, and post-signature tracking to ensure decisions are executed and expected value is realized.

3) GPO governance and relationship management

  • Support governance of CRLTC relationships by coordinating internal alignment on strategy, commitments, growth expectations, share-of-wallet objectives, and execution requirements.

  • Serve as a central point of coordination across internal teams to ensure GPO and Buying Group-related priorities, issues, data needs, and opportunities are surfaced, evaluated, and managed consistently.

  • Monitor commitments, milestones, market-share objectives, leakage-recapture priorities, and governance requirements; escalate risks or execution gaps that may affect partnership performance.

  • Support preparation for GPO business reviews, governance meetings, renewals, forecasting discussions, amendment planning, and strategic interactions.

  • Help ensure GPO partnerships are managed against enterprise objectives, customer commitments, profitability expectations, growth requirements, and long-term value.

4) Strategic Enterprise Engagement

  • Act as a strategic connector across Sales, Pricing, Commercial Finance, SmartSource, Strategic Global Sourcing, Supply Chain/USSC, Commercial Excellence, Legal/Contracting, segment leaders, and other enterprise stakeholders to build alignment on high-priority commercial matters.

  • Coordinate cross-functional input, competitive intelligence, market insight, customer feedback, and win/loss learnings to shape customer strategies, evaluate options, assess feasibility, and support timely decisions.

  • Develop fact-based views of customer profitability, Buying Group performance, purchasing behavior, share-of-wallet, leakage, market dynamics, and competitive position to inform enterprise priorities and leadership discussions.

  • Synthesize internal and external inputs into practical recommendations that strengthen CRLTC go-to-market strategy, partnership management, portfolio planning, and deal decision-making.

  • Prepare executive-ready summaries, recommendations, and discussion materials that elevate emerging risks, opportunities, and market dynamics for leadership consideration.

Experience and Educational Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Economics, Marketing, Healthcare Administration, or related field; advanced degree preferred.

  • Typically 10+ years of relevant experience in commercial strategy, deal governance, pricing/contracting, commercial finance, portfolio management, GPO management, or related roles within healthcare, pharmaceutical distribution, or a comparable B2B environment.

  • Experience supporting or leading commercial governance forums, strategic deal reviews, contract/renewal processes, and cross-functional decision-making.

  • Experience working with or supporting GPOs, Buying Groups, strategic customer partnerships, or other complex channel/customer structures is strongly preferred.

  • Strong understanding of commercial strategy principles, pricing frameworks, contract governance, and economic value drivers.

  • Strong analytical and financial acumen, with ability to evaluate deal economics, profitability, share-of-wallet, leakage, and contract performance, and communicate implications to senior leaders.

  • Demonstrated ability to influence and align stakeholders across a matrixed organization without direct authority.

  • Strong executive communication, meeting leadership, and material-development skills, including the ability to turn complex issues into concise, decision-ready recommendations.

  • Proven ability to manage multiple strategic priorities with strong organization, follow-through, and attention to detail

Minimum Skills, Knowledge and Ability:

  • High analytical horsepower and financial discipline, with the ability to convert data, assumptions, and commercial complexity into practical business recommendations

Based in Irvine, CA, PSD Underwear is a designer, marketer, and distributor of high quality, affordable, and premium briefs, boxers, sports bras, and loungewear. General Summary

PSD isn't built to be a brand that only shows up when we have something to sell.

We're looking for a Director, Social & Experiential to lead the part of PSD that keeps us connected to the consumer, culture and community every single day.

This role leads two critical workstreams: Social Media & Influencers and Events & Ambassadors and is fluent in culture knowledge and community building.

If Marketing Strategy owns much of the planned world, culture & community owns the part that doesn't fit neatly into a calendar. This is where PSD reacts to culture, finds the next thing, gets into the community, creates conversations and turns the brand into something people want to be part of.

You will build the strategy, lead the team and set the standard, but you also need to be a player. You should be comfortable capturing content, jumping into social, building relationships with creators, attending events, pitching ideas and figuring things out in real time.

This is the heartbeat of PSD..

What You’ll Own

Social & Cultural Strategy

  • Own PSD's organic social strategy and cultural point of view across platforms.
  • Build an always-on approach that keeps PSD culturally relevant and connected to our consumer.
  • Identify trends, creators, memes, communities, conversations and opportunities that can move the brand forward.
  • Establish platform-specific best practices and continually evolve how PSD shows up.
  • Partner with Marketing Strategy to ensure social and community insights inform larger campaign strategies.

Influencers & Creators

  • Build and lead PSD's influencer and creator strategy.
  • Identify creators who are culturally relevant and brand-right.
  • Develop creative partnerships that prioritize interesting ideas and organic reach over traditional paid endorsement.
  • Build long-term relationships with creators, tastemakers and communities.
  • Create a point of view on who PSD should be in culture and why.

Ambassadors

  • Build and evolve PSD's Ambassador program.
  • Develop a network of brand-right people who authentically represent PSD.
  • Create programs that drive both community and measurable commercial value.
  • Establish the distinction between creators we collaborate with and ambassadors who participate through affiliate relationships.
  • Develop systems that make the program scalable without losing authenticity.

Events & Community

  • Own the strategy for PSD's events and community presence.
  • Develop a portfolio of events and grassroots activations that make PSD matter beyond traditional marketing moments.

  • Ensure events are culturally relevant, experiential and rooted in the communities we're trying to serve.
  • Build relationships with local communities, schools, athletes, creators, venues and cultural partners.
  • Create a point of view on where PSD should show up and where we shouldn't.

Lead at the pace of culture

  • Be the person who sees something happening on Tuesday and asks, What can PSD do about this by Friday?
  • Move quickly without sacrificing brand quality.
  • Make decisions with imperfect information.
  • Create content and participate in the culture rather than simply observe it.
  • Know when something needs a plan and when it simply needs someone to go do it.

Lead and develop the team

  • Build and eventually lead a team of 4-5 across Social, Influencers, Events and Ambassadors.
  • Coach the team to be both strategically sharp and highly hands-on.
  • Establish a culture of experimentation, speed, accountability and creativity.
  • Raise the standard for how PSD participates in culture.

Who you Are

  • You know what people are talking about before it becomes a trend report.
  • You understand platforms because you actually create for them.
  • You know creators because you know their work, not because you have a spreadsheet of their follower counts.
  • Obsessed with Instagram, TikTok, YouTube and Discord (and willing to find new platforms to leverage)
  • You're creative, but you're also a leader.

Description

MEDvidi is an AI-powered mental healthcare platform setting a new standard for safe, effective, and scalable psychiatric care in the United States. We combine licensed providers with proprietary AI tools to deliver consistent, outcomes-driven treatment for conditions like ADHD, anxiety, depression, and more. MEDvidi's technology automates charting, follow-ups, and treatment planning, freeing providers to focus on patient care while improving efficiency and clinical quality.

As a product-focused Senior Frontend Developer on our AI track, you'll own frontend delivery end-to-end for products that directly affect how patients access mental health care and how our clinicians and staff work day-to-day. Your work sits at the intersection of a large, actively evolving Angular codebase and our AI-first product surface - patient-facing applications, internal tools for doctors and administrators, and the frontend for AI-powered features like our AI clinical assistant and AI receptionist. You'll work in a small cross-functional product team, taking features from requirement refinement through production release.

﻿Why this role:

  • Real product ownership in autonomous cross-functional team, you shape what gets built, not just how.
  • Deep hands-on work on AI-powered clinical and administrative products, with AI-assisted development as a first-class part of the engineering culture (Claude Code, Cursor, and beyond).
  • Modern Angular at scale: an actively evolving monorepo on the latest Angular versions, not a legacy graveyard.

Responsibilities

  • Design, develop, and maintain product features end-to-end within a cross-functional team, from requirement refinement to production release.
  • Take ownership of existing Angular codebase areas after the departing engineer: understand, stabilize, and improve them without slowing down the roadmap.
  • Write clean, maintainable, well-tested code: code reviews, unit tests (Vitest), and lightweight design documentation as part of the daily routine.
  • Contribute to frontend architecture decisions and platform health: performance, framework upgrades, NX monorepo structure, CI/CD improvements.
  • Drive AI adoption on both fronts: building frontend for AI-powered product features, and integrating AI tooling into the development workflow itself.
  • Actively contribute to the continuous improvement of engineering processes and tooling across the community.

﻿This role is not for you if:

  • You're waiting for someone else to define what to build,we expect you to come up with ideas, take them through discovery and development, ship them, and own the results after launch.
  • You need a fully-specced ticket queue and a PM/BA translating everything for you
  • You see AI coding agents as a novelty rather than a core part of how modern frontend work gets done.

Requirements

  • 3+ years of commercial experience with Angular(latest versions preferred).
  • Experience owning a product end-to-end, including analysing the metrics that tell you whether it actually worked.
  • Strong product and UX judgment, you can recognize when an interaction doesn't feel right and propose a better solution.
  • Fluency in modern Angular: standalone components, signals, current change detection and DI patterns, not experience from several years ago followed by a switch to another framework.
  • Advanced RxJS and TypeScript in real production scenarios: confident design and debugging of complex reactive flows (stream composition, cancellation, race conditions, error handling) and fluency in a strictly typed codebase.
  • Proven expertise in designing and implementing complex Angular application architectures at scale, module and component boundaries, decisions that hold up as the codebase grows.
  • Hands-on experience with unit testing (Vitest preferred, Jest acceptable) as a regular part of the daily routine, not an afterthought.
  • Hands-on experience with agentic AI development. For us this is a must, not a bonus: active daily use of coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, or similar), the ability to write effective skills, prompts, and instructions for them, understanding of the principles behind how agents operate (context, tools, feedback loops), and structuring code and documentation so agents can work with the codebase effectively.
  • Comfort working across the backend boundary: writing or fixing a SQL query, adjusting endpoint validation, or tracing an issue through the API layer. You don't need to be a backend engineer, but stopping at the frontend border isn't an option.
  • Intermediate English (B1+) and fluent Russian.
  • Full overlap with CET working hours.

Would be a plus:

  • Experience building UI for AI/LLM-powered features.
  • Deep understanding of responsive design, our patients access the platform primarily from mobile devices, and interfaces must be flawless across screen sizes.
  • Proficiency in optimizing web application performance across different surfaces: patient-facing product and internal tools for doctors, managers, and admins (data-heavy interfaces, large tables and lists, real-time updates).

What we offer

  • High-impact environment: A chance to contribute to a product-driven company in the medical tech space.
  • Growth & compensation: Clear growth opportunities and a competitive compensation package.
  • Remote-first: Fully remote long-term collaboration under a B2B model.

jobs.title: Senior Federal Pricing Manager
jobs.excerpt: The Challenge:JCTM is increasing the size, complexity, and strategic importance of the federal services opportunities it pursues across prime, subcontract, joint venture, IDIQ, GWAC, and task-order environments.
jobs.description:
The Challenge:

JCTM is increasing the size, complexity, and strategic importance of the federal services opportunities it pursues across prime, subcontract, joint venture, IDIQ, GWAC, and task-order environments. As our federal portfolio grows, JCTM is strengthening its pricing capability to bring competitive pricing analysis earlier into capture, improve proposal economics, protect execution feasibility, and give leadership better information for pursuit and investment decisions.

The successful candidate will be able to analyze available customer, competitor, labor-market, contract, and cost information and clearly explain: “Here is the likely competitive range, here is where our current price sits, here are the major drivers, here are the available levers, and here is the pricing approach I recommend.”

JCTM is looking for an experienced, hands-on federal pricing professional who understands that successful pricing goes beyond completing a cost model. This person will help JCTM understand what a competitive price may look like, how the proposed solution and staffing model affect that price, and what adjustments may improve both competitiveness and execution.

Build Your Career:

This role is an opportunity for an experienced Senior Pricing Analyst, Pricing Manager, Senior Pricing Manager, or similarly qualified federal pricing professional to take on greater ownership, work directly with senior leadership, and help mature JCTM’s strategic pricing capability. You will remain close to the work, building and reviewing pricing models, analyzing competitive ranges, evaluating staffing and labor assumptions, supporting BOEs, and pricing major federal pursuits, while gaining increased responsibility for pricing strategy and executive-level recommendations.

Challenging Projects:

As the Senior Federal Pricing Manager, you will lead hands-on pricing activities for significant federal pursuits and help mature JCTM’s competitive pricing and Price-to-Win capabilities. You will develop and evaluate pricing scenarios, conduct competitive pricing analysis, assess staffing and solution economics, review BOEs, and translate incomplete market and acquisition information into defensible recommendations.

Working with Growth, Capture, Finance, Operations, Proposal, Recruiting, HR, and technical SMEs, you will help leadership understand where JCTM’s proposed pricing sits relative to the competitive environment and identify practical levers that can improve competitiveness without undermining successful execution. This position offers significant visibility to JCTM leadership while providing room to grow into broader ownership of the company’s pricing strategy, processes, tools, and competitive-pricing infrastructure.

Key Responsibilities:

Federal Proposal Pricing & Financial Modeling

  • Independently develop, maintain, audit, and troubleshoot complex federal proposal pricing and financial models.
  • Develop pricing for labor-intensive federal professional services opportunities, including complex multi-year pursuits and task orders.
  • Support FFP, FFP-LOE, T&M/Labor Hour, CPFF/cost-reimbursable, IDIQ, GWAC, and task-order pricing environments.
  • Model and analyze direct labor, fully burdened rates, fringe, overhead, G&A, escalation, subcontractors, consultants, travel, ODCs, fee/profit, gross margin, and total contract value.
  • Perform mathematical, formula, compliance, reasonableness, and sensitivity checks before executive review and proposal submission.
  • Develop multiple executable pricing scenarios and clearly explain the financial, competitive, staffing, and margin implications of each.

Competitive Pricing & Price-to-Win Analysis

  • Conduct or materially contribute to Price-to-Win analyses for priority federal pursuits using both top-down and bottom-up methodologies.
  • Develop defensible likely competitive or winning ranges based on available customer, competitor, acquisition, labor-market, historical-award, and pricing information.
  • Clearly document assumptions, confidence levels, known facts, analytical estimates, and material uncertainties.
  • Compare JCTM’s estimated price against likely competitive ranges and identify the principal labor, staffing, indirect-rate, fee, subcontractor, workshare, and solution drivers creating variance.
  • Reconcile top-down competitive analysis with bottom-up solution and cost modeling.
  • Help mature JCTM’s approach to incorporating competitive pricing analysis earlier in capture as additional experience and intelligence are developed.

Capture, Qualification & Pricing Strategy

  • Engage with Capture before final RFP release when sufficient information exists to begin meaningful pricing analysis.
  • Evaluate draft RFPs, PWS/SOWs, RFIs, acquisition strategy, historical awards, incumbent position, customer budgets, evaluation methodology, staffing assumptions, and available competitive intelligence.
  • Use pricing and competitive intelligence to inform or influence capture strategy, staffing, teaming, solution design, and Bid/No-Bid decisions.
  • Identify and professionally challenge unsupported pricing, staffing, labor-mix, margin, teaming, and execution assumptions when the available analysis indicates a material concern.
  • Provide pricing analysis and recommendations for significant pursuits and participate in applicable gate and Bid/No-Bid reviews.

BOE, Solution Economics & Staffing Analysis

  • Work with technical, capture, proposal, and operations leaders to develop and review Basis of Estimate documentation.
  • Maintain alignment and traceability between solicitation requirements, technical solution, staffing plan, BOE, hours, labor categories, and pricing assumptions.
  • Work with Operations, Program Management, Recruiting, HR, and technical SMEs to develop defensible labor categories, labor mixes, staffing levels, hours, phasing, and rate assumptions.
  • Evaluate staffing models for competitiveness, affordability, and execution feasibility.
  • Identify areas where labor mix, experience bands, staffing levels, phasing, or teaming may be adjusted without undermining technical execution.

Competitive, Customer & Labor-Market Intelligence

  • Research federal award history, incumbent contracts, customer buying patterns, competitor positioning, probable competitor rates and indirect structures, market compensation, public job postings, BLS data, government databases, and available commercial market-intelligence sources.
  • Use partner and subcontractor intelligence when useful and validate material assumptions where practical.
  • Clearly distinguish known information, inferred information, and analytical estimates.
  • Help develop and maintain reusable competitor-pricing, labor-rate, historical-award, and competitive-pricing intelligence so lessons from each pursuit strengthen future pricing decisions.
  • Incorporate relevant win/loss and debrief information into future pricing analysis.

Teammate, Subcontractor & Workshare Pricing

  • Coordinate pricing inputs and data calls with subcontractors, teaming partners, consultants, and joint venture participants.
  • Evaluate teammate pricing for competitiveness, labor-category alignment, indirect treatment, escalation, ODCs, period-of-performance consistency, workshare requirements, and pass-through/margin impact.
  • Analyze the pricing implications of labor allocation, teammate rates, workshare, pass-through, and subcontractor economics.
  • Support teammate and subcontractor pricing discussions and negotiations as required.

Executive Pricing Communication

  • Prepare concise, decision-quality pricing analyses for Growth, Finance, Operations, and executive leadership.
  • Clearly communicate likely competitive pricing ranges, JCTM’s estimated pricing position, significant assumptions, key cost and staffing drivers, margin implications, uncertainties, and available pricing levers.
  • Recommend pricing approaches based on available evidence and explain the assumptions and tradeoffs underlying those recommendations.
  • Defend pricing recommendations under questioning and professionally challenge unsupported assumptions.

Compliance, Process & Pricing Infrastructure

  • Apply working knowledge of FAR, DFARS, federal acquisition requirements, and government contract pricing principles to pricing activities.
  • Support compliance with solicitation-specific pricing instructions and applicable requirements concerning allowability, allocability, reasonableness, labor standards, and cost or pricing data.
  • Help develop and improve pricing models, rate libraries, templates, assumption logs, review checklists, and version-control practices appropriate for a growing small/mid-market GovCon.
  • Protect proprietary, procurement-sensitive, source-selection-sensitive, and contractor bid/proposal information.
  • Help capture lessons from awards, losses, and debriefs to improve future pricing analysis and processes.

Room to Grow:

This position provides meaningful exposure to JCTM’s CEO, CGO, CFO, Capture leadership, Operations, and other key decision-makers. You will have the opportunity to take increasing ownership of JCTM’s pricing strategy and infrastructure as the company grows. A successful individual can help shape how JCTM approaches competitive pricing, opportunity qualification, capture strategy, pricing posture, and investment decisions. This role is particularly well suited for a strong Senior Pricing Analyst, Pricing Manager, Senior Pricing Manager, or comparable federal pricing professional who has performed substantive pricing work on major federal pursuits and is ready for greater ownership and executive visibility.

You Have:

  • 7+ years of progressively responsible federal government contracting pricing, cost analysis, proposal pricing, competitive pricing/Price-to-Win analysis, or closely related experience.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently own complex federal pricing models and proposal-pricing activities.
  • Experience conducting or materially contributing to federal competitive pricing/Price-to-Win analyses and developing defensible likely competitive or winning ranges.
  • Demonstrated ability to perform and reconcile top-down and bottom-up pricing analysis.
  • Significant experience pricing labor-intensive federal professional services.
  • Experience supporting significant federal services pursuits, including complex multi-year opportunities and task orders.
  • Advanced Microsoft Excel skills and the ability to independently build, audit, and troubleshoot complex pricing and financial models.
  • Strong understanding of labor-rate development, compensation markets, indirect rates, wrap, escalation, fee/profit, gross margin, and sensitivity analysis.
  • Experience developing and reviewing BOEs and aligning the technical solution, staffing, hours, and pricing assumptions.
  • Experience using pricing and competitive intelligence to inform or influence capture strategy, staffing, teaming, solution design, and Bid/No-Bid decisions.
  • Working knowledge of FAR, DFARS, federal acquisition requirements, and government contract pricing principles.
  • Strong communication skills and the ability to clearly explain and defend pricing recommendations under questioning and professionally challenge unsupported assumptions.
  • Ability to operate hands-on in a lean small/mid-market GovCon environment without requiring a large pricing department around you.
  • Ability to manage multiple concurrent pursuits and compressed proposal timelines.
  • Eligibility to obtain and maintain a U.S. government security clearance.

Nice to Haves:

  • Experience leading subcontractor or JV pricing, workshare analysis, rate comparison, and pricing negotiations.
  • Direct DoD and/or Intelligence Community pricing experience.
  • Experience with OASIS+, SeaPort-NxG, GSA MAS/Schedules, STARS, Polaris, or other GWAC/IDIQ and task-order environments.
  • Experience working with joint ventures and mentor-protégé arrangements.
  • Experience pricing 8(a), SDVOSB, small-business set-aside, and other socioeconomic acquisition strategies.
  • Knowledge of limitations on subcontracting and small-business workshare requirements.
  • Experience with LPTA and best-value tradeoff evaluation strategies.
  • Experience participating in Black Hat, competitive assessment, pre-RFP capture, and formal gate-review processes.
  • Experience with GovWin or comparable federal market-intelligence tools and public award/compensation databases.
  • Experience with Deltek Costpoint/GCS, Unanet, JAMIS, or comparable GovCon accounting/ERP platforms.
  • Experience responding to DCAA, DCMA, or government pricing information requests.
  • Experience helping build or materially improve a corporate pricing capability, model library, competitive-intelligence repository, or formal competitive-pricing process.

Compensation:

JCTM is committed to fair and transparent compensation practices. The anticipated compensation for this position will be determined based on a variety of job-related factors, which may include the candidate’s relevant education, training, certifications, security clearance and access requirements, years and depth of relevant experience, specialized skills and qualifications, position level, assigned responsibilities, work location, applicable contract or customer requirements, internal equity, and the approved compensation budget for the position. Where required by applicable state or local law, JCTM will include the applicable good-faith salary or hourly pay range, along with any required information regarding benefits and other compensation, in the job posting.

Equal Opportunity Employer Statement:

JCTM is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

jobs.description:
Senior Health PFM Advisor*

Deadline: 1pm (GMT) on 22 October 2026.

*IBP is recruiting for this position in anticipation of funding. Any offer of employment will be conditional upon the required funding being confirmed

Contract length: Full-Time (Initial 1-year fixed-term contract, with view to renew).

Location: IBP's team currently works across a range of time zones, with many colleagues based between UTC-5 and UTC+3. We encourage applications from anywhere, though we take into account time zone compatibility and proximity to our country offices.

Annual salary: IBP Salaries are set with consideration of current market conditions and in comparison with similar not-for-profit organizations. Based on current rates, we would anticipate a gross salary to be offered as per the below locations. *Please note these locations are given to illustrate specific country salary ranges. The salary offered will be payable in local currency, based on local markets and commensurate with experience.

    • USD41,475 - 43,430 per annum in Nigeria
    • CFA 26,156,180 - 29,214,581 per annum in Senegal
    • ZAR 789,698 - 826,908 per annum in South Africa
    • KES 4,348,190 - 4,553,080 per annum in Kenya
    • EUR 65,000 - 80,000 per annum in Europe

Preferred start date: January 2027

Physical demands: Regional and in-country travel will be required. This is a remote role, with prolonged working on a laptop and other display screen equipment around 8 hours each day.

Reports to: Global Lead, Policy and Research

Background

Around the world, public resources are being raised and spent unfairly and ineffectively, leaving millions of people without access to quality public goods and services they need to thrive. Governments often make public resource decisions without much consultation or information from the public. Meanwhile, those with power and privilege very effectively influence government decisions in their favors.

Our goal is to make governments raise and spend public money more fairly, so that everyone has the resources and opportunities they need to thrive and get ahead. To achieve this, The International Budget Partnership (IBP) partners with budget analysts, community organizers, and advocates in more than 100 countries to advance public budget systems that work for people.

Together, we generate evidence, advocate for reform, and build the skills and knowledge of people so that everyone can have a voice in budget decisions that impact their lives. For more information, please visit our website and review our strategy.

Today, IBP is a globally dispersed organization with staff based in multiple countries with in-depth country work in Nigeria, South Africa, Indonesia, and Francophone Africa. IBP is a US registered 501 c3 with branch offices in Senegal and affiliates in the Netherlands, in South Africa and in Nigeria and a total budget of about USD 14 million a year.

In addition to our in-depth country work, IBP works with partners in more than 30 countries to strengthen budget transparency, participation, and accountability. Although IBP is not a sector-focused organization, in recent years we have focused on specific sectors, such as health and water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), in selected countries.

Health public financial management (health PFM) concerns how public resources are planned, budgeted, released, spent, reported, and overseen within the health sector. IBP is building a portfolio of technical assistance, capacity strengthening, research, and country-level programming focused on improving the credibility, execution, transparency, and accountability of health spending.

IBP combines a problem-driven approach to PFM reform with an accountability ecosystem approach. Rather than beginning with generic assessments of compliance with good practice, we work with country teams, civil society, government, and other stakeholders to identify concrete problems affecting health spending and service delivery; diagnose their fiscal, institutional, operational, and political causes; and identify feasible ways to address the most important bottlenecks. At the same time, we examine the wider accountability ecosystem around these problems, including the roles, relationships, incentives, and influence of finance and health institutions, oversight bodies, civil society, communities, and development partners. This can include problems with budget releases and execution, resource flows to frontline facilities, procurement and cash management, or coordination and accountability across institutions. Our multi-country work also allows us to identify common problems, share lessons across countries, and engage with regional and global institutions to inform health financing policy and practice beyond individual countries.

About this role

IBP is seeking a senior technical professional to provide technical expertise for its growing health PFM portfolio. The Advisor will provide direct technical assistance and capacity strengthening to country teams and civil society partners; help teams diagnose and address problems in how health resources are planned, budgeted, released, spent, and accounted for; and develop the research methods and diagnostic tools that ground this work in evidence.

The role requires a strong PFM practitioner who can work across health and finance systems and move between hands-on technical support, applied research and diagnosis, and facilitation of problem-solving among diverse actors. The Advisor will help teams understand why specific PFM problems occur and how the institutions, incentives, relationships, and accountability mechanisms surrounding them can enable or constrain reform.

The successful candidate will be able to translate this analysis into feasible strategies for reform and stronger accountability.

Role responsibilities

Essential duties of the job include, but are not limited to, the following:

1. Technical Assistance and Capacity Strengthening (50%)

  • Provide direct technical assistance to regional and country teams and partners, with a focus on Africa but also covering IBP’s broader partner engagements on health budgets, to diagnose and address health PFM problems, including budget credibility and execution, resource flows, procurement, expenditure controls, reporting, and other constraints affecting the translation of budgets into services.
  • Help teams identify the technical, institutional, and political causes of identified problems; map the actors, relationships, incentives, and accountability mechanisms that shape them; and develop feasible strategies for addressing them.
  • Facilitate technical dialogue and joint problem-solving among finance/budget and health institutions, subnational governments, civil society, oversight institutions, communities, development partners, and other relevant actors, helping identify where collaboration, oversight, or citizen engagement can contribute to reform.
  • Design and deliver capacity strengthening and training for IBP teams, civil society partners, government counterparts, and other accountability actors.
  • Facilitate technical dialogue and joint problem-solving among finance/budget and health institutions, subnational governments, civil society, oversight institutions, development partners, and other relevant actors.
  • Provide ongoing technical advice and facilitation to IBP teams and partners in English, and in French where possible.

2. Research and Methodology Development (30%)

  • Develop and refine practical research methods and diagnostic approaches that combine analysis of specific health PFM problems with analysis of the accountability ecosystems surrounding them, drawing where appropriate on IBP's Open Budget Survey and complementary PFM and health-sector data and tools.
  • Conduct or oversee country-level analysis that combines quantitative budget and expenditure data with institutional and political economy analysis to explain why implementation problems occur, which actors and incentives shape them, and where opportunities for reform and stronger accountability exist.
  • Conduct or oversee country-level analysis of health budget credibility, execution, resource flows, reporting, and oversight, combining quantitative analysis with institutional and political economy analysis to explain why implementation problems occur.
  • Translate findings into actionable recommendations, technical briefs, diagnostic reports, and other products that support country-level problem-solving, reform, and advocacy.
  • Identify recurring problems and evidence gaps across countries and use lessons from implementation to strengthen IBP's health PFM methodologies and technical assistance.

3. Coordination and Strategic Alignment (20%)

  • Work with IBP's Global Policy and Partnerships team, country Policy Leads, and Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning colleagues to integrate health PFM expertise into country programming, connect learning across countries, and align the work with IBP's broader strategy.
  • Coordinate work planning, budgets, and reporting for assigned health PFM projects and activities.
  • Represent IBP's health PFM work with donors, government counterparts, technical partners, and relevant policy and technical forums.
  • Contribute technical content to concept notes, funding proposals, and donor reports.
  • Actively engage and contribute to team meetings, staff meetings, other coordination meetings, and other assigned tasks as required.

Core Competencies/experience

  • Minimum 7 years of professional experience providing technical assistance, advisory support, or applied analysis on public financial management, including experience in the health sector.
  • Strong technical understanding of PFM systems, particularly budget formulation, program budgeting, budget credibility and execution, resource tracking and financing systems, expenditure controls, and financial reporting, and demonstrated ability to apply this knowledge to practical implementation problems.
  • Understanding of health systems and health financing and how they interact with government PFM systems. Direct health PFM or health financing experience is strongly preferred.
  • Demonstrated ability to diagnose complex PFM problems using quantitative, institutional, and political economy analysis, including analysis of the actors, incentives, relationships, and accountability mechanisms that shape implementation, and translate findings into feasible strategies for action.
  • Experience providing hands-on technical assistance for government, civil society, and/or other country-level actors, with experience designing and delivering capacity strengthening also preferred.
  • Experience developing or adapting research methods, diagnostic tools, or analytical frameworks for country-level PFM or sectoral analysis.
  • Strong facilitation and communication skills, including the ability to convene actors with different institutional perspectives and communicate complex PFM issues clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Extensive experience working across countries and cultures, including engagement with governments, civil society organizations, development partners, and other stakeholders in low- and middle-income countries.
  • Commitment to equity and social justice and to strengthening citizen and civil society participation in public resource decision-making and accountability.
  • Fluency in English required. Working knowledge of French and familiarity with francophone PFM systems, such as the WAEMU (UEMOA) harmonized public finance framework, are an advantage.

How to apply and key dates

Please complete the online application form, including the short screening questions, submit your CV and provide a cover letter that provides tangible examples of how your skills, knowledge and experience will support your ability to perform the key priorities outlined in the above job description (using no more than 750 words).

Please include as website links in your cover letter, or as attachments to your application, at least two examples of technical assistance, training materials, or written work that relate to health, PFM, or budget accountability.

The recruitment process will involve a technical panel interview and a final panel interview.

First round interviews are planned for the weeks of 2 and 9 November 2026, with final interviews planned for the week of 16 November 2026.

jobs.description:
Position Summary

The Implementation and Evaluation (I&E) Team guides KnowledgeWorks in charting a clear, evidence-informed path that helps advance and refine our strategy in pursuit of equitable, meaningful outcomes. The I&E team promotes calibration to what’s working and identifies what isn’t or what needs to shift. We align project implementation with strong evaluation practices to generate actionable insights, mitigate risk, build capacity, and promote continuous learning. We cultivate alignment across teams by modeling a culture of curiosity, collaboration, and continuous improvement to move in a shared direction toward our collective goals. Using our data and evaluation expertise, we measure KnowledgeWorks’ impact and enable our geographies to use data, advance the quality of KnowledgeWorks research and evaluation work, and support the use of KnowledgeWorks data infrastructure.

The Manager, Data Operations and Insights is part of the I&E team and reports to the Director, Strategic Impact and Learning. This is an ideal position for someone who thrives in bringing order to complexity; connecting people with the information they need; and building systems that help teams learn, collaborate, and make better decisions. This position coordinates data operations, knowledge management, and insight-sharing efforts that turn information into actionable knowledge and strengthen organizational learning and impact.

This position exercises discretion and independent judgment with respect to matters of significance.

As part of the larger KnowledgeWorks team, this position will actively participate in our ongoing diversity, equity, inclusion and justice work. We are reflecting and improving our internal culture, as well as growing our competencies to effectively engage in education systems change with our partners. Engaging in this work is an essential part of each team member’s personal professional development, external capability building and contribution to the culture and work of KnowledgeWorks.

Core Responsibilities

KNOWLEDGE MANAGEMENT & INSIGHTS ENABLEMENT

  • Co-lead and help build the structure, upkeep, and usability of the I&E team’s knowledge management and evidence-sharing systems, including an Insights Hub and other repositories of evaluation, implementation, and learning assets.
  • Ensure that data, insights, tools, and related documentation are organized, accessible, and maintained in ways that support continuity, reduce ad hoc work and strengthen institutional memory.
  • Support the development of repeatable insight products, summaries, and synthesis materials—including board and impact reports—that help make I&E team findings more usable across the organization.
  • Prepare and organize information that supports internal sensemaking, insight-sharing, and decision-making processes.
  • Support the handoff from analysis and evaluation outputs to broader team and organizational use.

DATA MANAGEMENT, GOVERNANCE, & WORKFLOW STEWARDSHIP

  • Steward day-to-day data workflows that support the collection, organization, storage, documentation, and use of data, including the storage and access of evaluation instruments.
  • Develop, maintain, and improve standard operating procedures, documentation, and shared norms related to data management and use.
  • Support effective data governance practices, including attention to data quality, validation, access, documentation, and responsible use of AI-enabled tools.
  • Help ensure that the team’s data practices are consistent, efficient, and aligned with evolving organizational needs and priorities.
  • Coordinate with internal partners, including IT and others, to communicate team needs related to data systems, workflows, and infrastructure—helping translate program and evaluation needs into clear requirements.

DATA PROJECT COORDINATION & INTERNAL WORK MANAGEMENT

  • Coordinate timelines, workflows, dependencies, and deliverables across data-, evaluation- and insights-related projects and workstreams.
  • Support the rollout and coordination of key frameworks and evaluation efforts (e.g., results framework) by helping organize the process, track next steps, and clarify roles and handoffs.
  • Support planning, tracking, and follow-through for assigned projects by helping to clarify next steps, roles, handoffs, and project-related needs.
  • Help manage internal teamwork processes and priorities connected to this role’s portfolio in order to strengthen coordination and reduce inefficiencies.
  • Support coordination with external research, evaluation, and data-related partners, including helping to clarify scopes of work, deliverables, and timelines.
  • Maintain project documentation and provide regular updates, status tracking, and other coordination support as needed to move work forward effectively.

CROSS-FUNCTIONAL INTEGRATION & TEAM/ORGANIZATIONAL SUPPORT

  • Contribute to I&E team priorities, processes, and continuous improvement efforts.
  • Support cross-functional collaboration by working with other KnowledgeWorks teams to strengthen alignment, information-sharing, and the effective use of data and insights.
  • Participate in team meetings, cross-team meetings, organizational meetings, and other collaborative structures as needed.
  • Contribute to special projects, pilots, or organizational efforts that benefit from strong coordination, documentation, or data stewardship.
  • Serve on ad hoc or standing committees, as assigned, in support of team and organizational priorities.

Education and Experience

  • 5+ years of relevant experience in areas such as data management, project/program coordination, knowledge management, and/or applied research or evaluation support; OR
  • Bachelor's degree in a related field (e.g., data or information management, education, social science, public administration, or a related discipline) and 3+ years of relevant experience; OR
  • Master's degree in a related field and 1+ years of relevant experience

Within your first 30 days you will:

  • Gain an understanding of KnowledgeWorks’ mission, programmatic offerings, and strategic priorities
  • Gain familiarity with KnowledgeWorks’ current data and knowledge management tools, processes, and structures
  • Start to establish relationships with key internal staff, within the I&E team and across other teams

Within your first 60 days you will:

  • Deepen understanding of the I&E team’s data management and project documentation practices and start to identify gaps and opportunities
  • Establish a working relationship with the staff leading KnowledgeWorks’ data infrastructure project
  • Collaborate on the initial development of a data workflow inventory (i.e., identify and catalog KnowledgeWorks’ current data workflows)
  • Develop initial set of recommendations for I&E team standard operating procedures related to data management and use

Within your first 6 months you will:

  • Co-develop an initial draft model for an Insights hub (or other repository) for centralizing data, implementation, and learning assets
  • Identify key data system and infrastructure requirements needed to house and share key organizational insights
  • Develop processes for the creation of repeatable insights products, such as impact reports and summary/synthesis materials
  • Meaningfully contribute to the standardization and improvement of the I&E team’s systems and processes

What KnowledgeWorks Can Offer You:

  • Flexible Schedule
  • Cell Phone Stipend
  • 401K Match Program
  • Employee Assistance Program
  • Matching Gifts Program

If you don’t meet every single requirement listed, we encourage you to apply anyway. Studies have shown that candidates with diverse backgrounds and experiences are less likely to apply to postings where they don’t meet every qualification exactly as written. KnowledgeWorks is committed to building a diverse, inclusive and authentic workplace that fuels our innovation.

KnowledgeWorks prohibits discrimination against qualified individuals based on their status as protected veterans or individuals with disabilities and prohibits discrimination against all individuals based on their age, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or national origin.

Moreover, KnowledgeWorks takes affirmative action to employ and advance in employment individuals without regard to age, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or veteran status.

jobs.description:
Position Only Available to Residents of Florida, Georgia, South Carolina, North Carolina, Virginia, Texas, Utah, Idaho, Tennessee, Missouri, Ohio, or Arizona.

We're on a mission to help the world work Anywhere. Whether working from home, an office, or Anywhere, we offer products and services designed to help people work and learn together, whether they're across a table or across the world. Work is what we do, not where we do it.

We're hiring Client Experience Associates to join our team!


Your Role

  • Watch first:A Day in the Life of a Client Experience Associate

  • Answer inbound calls for our clients' businesses from home. You'll capture leads, take orders, schedule appointments, and send messages to clients.

  • Handle a range of call types, including standard answering, Active Response (where a message pops up and you are to make an outbound call to someone), live chat, relay calls, appointment setting, and legal intake calls. You'll be trained on each one.

  • Expect a steady, fast pace. Calls often come in back-to-back, and we measure performance by quality, accuracy, ready %, and after-call work time.

Your Schedule

  • 40 hours per week, mostly scheduled between 5:00 am and 8:00 pm Pacific Time.

  • A minimum of 8 hours every Friday and Saturday is required for the first 8-12 weeks after training.

  • You choose your own shifts each week, but choice is ranked by performance tier. Higher tiers pick first, so new associates should expect the least choice at the start. Flexibility is a must.

  • Attendance is tracked with a points system. Being reliable is very important!

Training

  • 2 weeks of paid training, followed by 8–12 weeks of Learning & Development, where you’ll take live calls with ongoing support.

  • During this period, you'll need full availability for 40 hours a week and can't block off holidays or vacation time.

Your Skills

  • Excellent verbal and written communication

  • A warm, upbeat tone and a genuine interest in helping people

  • A good listener who stays calm and efficient under pressure

  • Dependable: you show up for every scheduled shift, on time

  • Strong computer skills and typing at a minimum of 30 WPM

  • A growth mindset and eagerness to learn new call types and tools

Requirements

Compensation & Benefits

  • Starting at $16.00/hour

  • Benefits start after 60 days: [e.g., medical, dental, vision, EAP, PTO]

  • 401(k) with matching after one year of employment

Your System

We use a Bring Your Own Device policy. Your computer and internet connection must meet oursystem and internet requirements before you start.

About AnywhereWorks

Work is what you do, not where you do it. We’re on a mission to help the world work Anywhere. We believe people should be able to work and learn together, whether they’re communicating across a table or across the world.

We offer a diverse set of products and services to a variety of businesses, from live answering services to scheduling and payment platforms to shared working spaces. We empower people to communicate, collaborate and produce. We’re committed to building a more inclusive future of work, where people can contribute from Anywhere.

What "Anywhere" Means to Us

Other terms out in the world are “remote” “distributed” “telecommuting” – for us, these words do not speak to the experience we hope you will have working with us Anywhere.

Isolation and a lack of social interaction are common concerns when people think about Remote working. The word “Remote” itself can conjure up ideas of loneliness and being disconnected from your colleagues. That’s why we like the more empowering language of “working Anywhere”, with Anywhere representing an unconstrained, plugged-in destination.

Background Check

Please note that all candidates who receive a conditional offer of employment will be required to undergo a background check as part of the pre-employment screening process. This is to ensure the safety and integrity of our workplace and to comply with our company policies.

We comply with all requirements of the Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA) to ensure the privacy and rights of our applicants are protected.

Equal Opportunity

AnywhereWorks is committed to providing equal opportunity employment; creating, managing, and valuing diversity in our workforce; providing a safe work environment; and fostering a culture of belonging where all employees are included, treated with dignity and respect, promoted on their merits, and placed in positions to contribute to our future success.

jobs.excerpt: Who we areFounded in 1999 and headquartered in Central Ohio, we’re a privately-owned, independent healthcare navigation organization.
jobs.description:
Who we are

Founded in 1999 and headquartered in Central Ohio, we’re a privately-owned, independent healthcare navigation organization. We believe that no one should have to navigate the cost and complexity of healthcare alone, and we’re on a mission to make healthcare simpler and more effective for our millions of members. Our big-hearted, tech-savvy team fights to ensure that our members get the care they need, when they need it, at the most affordable cost – that’s why we call ourselves Healthcare Warriors®.

We’re committed to building diverse and inclusive teams – more than 2,000 of us and counting – so if you’re excited about this position, we encourage you to apply – even if your experience doesn’t match every requirement.

Job Summary

Quantum Health is seeking a strategic and results-driven Product Marketing Manager to help shape and execute our go-to-market strategy. In this role, you will bridge the gap between market needs, client insights, and product innovation, ensuring our solutions are positioned effectively and clearly differentiated in the healthcare and benefits marketplace.

As a key member of the marketing team, you will be responsible for developing product positioning and messaging, creating impactful marketing assets, supporting product launches, and equipping sales and client-facing teams with the tools they need to succeed. You will collaborate closely with Product, Technology, Sales, Marketing, and Client teams to communicate the value of our solutions and reinforce Quantum Health's position as an industry innovator.

The ideal candidate brings a combination of strategic thinking and hands-on execution, along with experience in healthcare, insurance, or employee benefits. This individual thrives in a fast-paced, high-growth environment and is passionate about translating complex concepts into compelling, customer-focused stories.

Essential Roles and Responsibilities

Market & Product Strategy

  • Develop a strong understanding of the healthcare and employee benefits landscape, including market dynamics and competitive trends.
  • Partner with Product Management, Sales, and Client teams to create differentiated positioning and messaging that resonates with employers, consultants, and other key buyers.
  • Provide market and competitive insights that inform product strategy, enhancements, and innovation initiatives.

Go-to-Market Execution

  • Lead marketing plans for assigned products and solutions, ensuring alignment with sales objectives and broader business goals.
  • Develop and maintain compelling sales and marketing collateral, including presentations, one-pagers, case studies, and other product-focused materials.
  • Support product launches through coordinated messaging, training, and multi-channel campaigns.
  • Translate complex product features and capabilities into clear, client- and member-centric benefits.

Sales Enablement & Internal Collaboration

  • Partner with Sales and Client-facing teams to develop training, tools, and resources that help articulate product value and drive adoption.
  • Collaborate closely with Partner Marketing, Demand Generation, Client Marketing, and Digital teams to ensure messaging is consistent and integrated across all channels.
  • Gather and analyze feedback from clients, prospects, and consultants to identify insights that inform future marketing strategies and product decisions.

Measurement & Continuous Improvement

  • Monitor and evaluate the effectiveness of product marketing initiatives, adjusting strategies to maximize impact and business results.
  • Support thought leadership efforts by identifying opportunities to showcase Quantum Health's value, innovation, and differentiation in the marketplace.

Skills and Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Communications, Business, Public Health, or a related field; equivalent experience will be considered.
  • 5-7+ years of marketing experience, preferably within healthcare, insurance, employee benefits, or a related industry.
  • Strong understanding of strategic marketing planning and tactical execution.
  • Excellent writing, editing, and presentation development skills.
  • Proven ability to translate complex information into clear, compelling, and customer-focused messaging.
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, including PowerPoint, Word, and Excel.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously, prioritize effectively, and deliver results.
  • Strong interpersonal and collaboration skills with the ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders.
  • Strategic mindset coupled with a proactive, hands-on approach to execution.
  • Ability to travel occasionally for conferences, industry events, and client meetings.

What’s in it for you:

  • Compensation: Competitive base and incentive compensation
  • Coverage: Health, vision and dental featuring our best-in-class healthcare navigation services, along with life insurance, legal and identity protection, adoption assistance, EAP, Teladoc services and more.
  • Retirement: 401(k) plan with up to 4% employer match and full vesting on day one.
  • Balance: Paid Time Off (PTO), 7 paid holidays, parental leave, volunteer days, paid sabbaticals, and more.
  • Development: Tuition reimbursement up to $5,250 annually, certification/continuing education reimbursement, discounted higher education partnerships, paid trainings and leadership development.
  • Culture: Recognition as a Best Place to Work for 15+ years, dedication to diversity, philanthropy and sustainability, and people-first values that drive every decision.
  • Environment: A modern workplace with a casual dress code, open floor plans, full-service dining, free snacks and drinks, complimentary 24/7 fitness center with group classes, outdoor walking paths, game room, notary and dry-cleaning services and more!

What you should know:

  • Internal Associates: Already a Healthcare Warrior? Apply internally through Lever
  • Process: Application > Recruiter Video Interview > Online Assessment(s) > Interview(s) > Offer > Background Check.
  • Diversity, Equity and Inclusion: Quantum Health welcomes everyone. We value our diverse team and suppliers, we’re committed to empowering our ERGs, and we’re proud to be an equal opportunity employer .
  • Tobacco-Free Campus: To further enable the health and wellbeing of our associates and community, Quantum Health maintains a tobacco-free environment. The use of all types of tobacco products is prohibited in all company facilities and on all company grounds.
  • Compensation Ranges: Compensation details published by job boards are estimates and not verified by Quantum Health. Details surrounding compensation will be disclosed throughout the interview process. Compensation offered is based on the candidate’s unique combination of experience and qualifications related to the position.
  • Sponsorship: Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States on a permanent and ongoing future basis without requiring sponsorship.
  • Agencies: Quantum Health does not accept unsolicited resumes or outreach from third-parties. Absent a signed MSA and request/approval from Talent Acquisition to submit candidates for a specific requisition, we will not approve payment to any third party.

Reasonable Accommodation:

Should you require reasonable accommodation(s) to participate in the application/interview/selection process, or in order to complete the essential duties of the position upon acceptance of a job offer, click here to submit a recruitment accommodation request.

Recruiting Scams:

Unfortunately, scams targeting job seekers are common. To protect our candidates, we want to remind you that authorized representatives of Quantum Health will only contact you from an email address ending in @quantum-health.com. Quantum Health will never ask for personally identifiable information such as Date of Birth (DOB), Social Security Number (SSN), banking/direct/tax details, etc. via email or any other non-secure system, nor will we instruct you to make any purchases related to your employment. If you believe you’ve encountered a recruiting scam, report it to the Federal Trade Commission and your state’s Attorney General.

California Employee and Job Applicant Notice of Collection of Personal Information:

If you are a California resident, Quantum Health may collect personal information in connection with your application for employment and, if hired, during the course of your employment. The categories of personal information collected and the purposes for which that information is used are described in our California Employee and Job Applicant Notice of Collection of Personal Information.

Please review the notice here:

California Employee and Job Applicant Notice

Use of Technology Notice:

Quantum Health and its authorized service providers may contact applicants by email, phone, and text message about their application and related employment opportunities. Text messages may cover application status, interview invitations, and reminders, and applicants will have the option to opt out at any time. Message frequency varies. Message and data rates may apply.

Quantum Health uses AI-assisted recruiting technology to support communication, scheduling, and candidate evaluation, including tools that may review application materials and analyze recorded interviews. These tools assist our recruiting team; final employment decisions are made by human reviewers. Applicants who will be interviewed using these tools receive advance notice describing the technology and what it evaluates, are asked for permission before the interview is recorded or analyzed, and may request deletion of their recording.

About the Role

SmartScale360 is hiring an experienced General Executive Assistant to provide high-level administrative, operational, and executive support to a fast-growing U.S.-based business.

This role is ideal for a highly organized and proactive professional who can manage competing priorities, coordinate schedules and communications, support day-to-day operations, and assist with light bookkeeping and financial administrative tasks.

You'll work closely with executives, clients, vendors, and internal teams to keep workflows organized, deadlines on track, and business operations running smoothly.

What You'll Do

  • Provide direct administrative support to executives and leadership, including managing priorities, documentation, and day-to-day workflows
  • Manage complex calendars, meetings, and appointments, including scheduling, prioritization, and coordination
  • Manage emails and communications by filtering messages, handling follow-ups, and maintaining clear communication with internal and external stakeholders
  • Answer, screen, and route phone calls professionally while ensuring timely communication and follow-up
  • Coordinate meetings, events, and business activities, including scheduling, preparation, logistics, and post-event follow-up
  • Assist with light bookkeeping and financial administrative tasks, including organizing transactions, receipts, invoices, and expenses
  • Support accounts payable and accounts receivable tracking, including payment follow-ups and maintaining accurate financial records
  • Assist with basic reconciliation and financial reporting as needed
  • Maintain organized spreadsheets, reports, trackers, and administrative records to support business operations
  • Track projects, deadlines, deliverables, and action items to ensure timely completion
  • Support ongoing operational projects and process improvements to increase efficiency and organization
  • Liaise with clients, vendors, and internal teams and assist executives in maintaining strong professional relationships
  • Follow up with stakeholders to ensure tasks, deliverables, and commitments are completed on time
  • Maintain confidential business and financial information with professionalism and discretion

What We're Looking For

  • 3–5 years of experience as an Executive Assistant, Virtual Assistant, Administrative Coordinator, Operations Coordinator, or similar role
  • Proven experience supporting executives, business owners, or leadership teams
  • Strong organizational, multitasking, and time-management skills
  • Excellent written and verbal English communication skills
  • Strong attention to detail and accuracy
  • Experience with basic bookkeeping or accounting administrative tasks
  • Strong proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including organizing data, creating spreadsheets and trackers, using basic formulas, and preparing reports
  • Experience with or a strong preference for using Notion for task management, documentation, databases, and workflow organization
  • Familiarity with CRM and project management platforms
  • Familiarity with social media management tools and platforms
  • Proactive, resourceful, and able to work independently in a remote environment
  • Comfortable handling confidential business and financial information
  • Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities
  • Able to learn and adapt quickly to new tools, systems, and processes

Tools You'll Use

  • Accounting/Bookkeeping: QuickBooks, Xero, or similar platforms
  • Productivity: Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, Google Workspace, Microsoft Office
  • Task Management & Documentation:Notion (preferred)
  • CRM: HubSpot, Salesforce, or similar platforms
  • Project Management: Asana, Trello, Monday.com, ClickUp, or similar
  • Communication: Slack, Zoom, Google Workspace, Microsoft Teams
  • Social Media: Meta Business Suite, Buffer, Hootsuite, or similar platforms

Work-From-Home Requirements

  • Laptop/PC: Intel i5 (or equivalent) with at least 8GB RAM
  • Internet: Stable 100 Mbps connection
  • Backup: Secondary internet connection, backup device, and reliable power source
  • Work Environment: Professional, quiet, and suitable for client-facing work

Schedule

  • Work Schedule: To be confirmed by the client
